item.title: [DF-792] Add Service Principals for MMS, Energy Aspects, Argus, Blather, WoodMac, and Keyera Price Deck.
item.description:
Creating this user story to add the Service Principals that are going to own the respective tables/jobs. Service Principals:

  • MMS
  • Energy Aspects
  • Argus
  • Blather
  • WoodMac
  • Keyera Price Deck

This will improve security and ownership clarity of the secured tables.

Acceptance Criteria:

  1. There is a service principal for the following data sources:
    1. MMS
    2. Energy Aspects
    3. Argus
    4. Blather
    5. WoodMac
    6. Keyera Price Deck
  2. Existing jobs should have their runners changed to the created SP:
    1. Energy Aspects
    2. Argus
    3. Blather
    4. WoodMac
    5. Keyera Price Deck
  3. Ensure the following SP have access to their secrets scopes for bronze ingestion:
    1. Argus
    2. Energy Aspects
    3. MMS
    4. Blather
item.summary: Add Service Principals for MMS, Energy Aspects, Argus, Blather, WoodMac, and Keyera Price Deck.

item.title: [DF-782] Add UOM column to the Meter Hierarchy table
item.description:
As a Plant Accounting, I need to see the UOM applicable to each meter on the TIPS meter hierarchy.

Technical details:

  1. Add a column, titled “UOM” to the meter hierarchy table (keyera_enterprise_prod.gold_tips.meter_hierarchy). The column needs to appear between the DIPS_CD and the GOVT_CD columns.
  2. For each line on the meter hierarchy table, determine the TIPS UOM by finding a matching combination of PROD_CD and DISP_CD in the keyera_enterprise_prod.gold_tips_reference.contractual_uom and its corresponding qty_uom_cd. If mutiple matches are found, use the most recent value based on the updt_dt value in the keyera_enterprise_prod.gold_tips_reference.contractual_uom table.

Acceptance criteria:

  • The Meter Hierarchy table includes the UOM column.
  • The UOM column includes correct UOM for each meter, derived from the combination of PROD_CD and DISP_CD for that meter, based on the keyera_enterprise_prod.gold_tips_reference.contractual_uom table

  • Terraform is Updated (to create resource dependencies like groups, Service Principals, catalogs, schemas, etc.)
  • Development Deployment is Validated
  • Story is Attached to a Release
  • Release is Deployed to Test

item.title: [DF-759] Dashboards do not run on Schedule when assigned to TerraForm created Compute
item.description:
Databricks allows for dashboards to be scheduled and subscribed to through the UI:

[Manage scheduled dashboard updates and subscriptions | Databricks on AWS|https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/dashboards/schedule-subscribe]

The KAPS Daily Volume Report dashboard in Commercial production was using this functionality without issue for a number of months. It is published using embedded credentials (lee_pattison98@keyera.com) which are part of the Workspace Admin group.

It started failing silently about a week or two ago. I noticed when I did not see the PDF email sent out. Upon investigation, I noticed (this is a hypothesis only, please treat as such) that if the compute cluster was not running when the schedule triggered the dashboard could not refresh. If the compute cluster was running, it sometimes worked and I could see the dashboard queries when looking at the cluster monitoring details.

I have been able to restore functionality by creating a new compute resource (SQL Warehouse - Databricks) that lee_pattison98@keyera.com owns, not terrform, and assign it when setting up the schedule.

To replicate:

Subscribe to both schedules' setup for: KAPS Daily Volume Report

  • 9 AM - this one uses a non-terraform owned cluster and should work. You should be able to see the query details if you look at the cluster monitoring results and you should receive and email.
  • Broken Schedule - this one uses a terraform cluster (Business Development | LIN | Analyst Cluster). This was selected as usually no one is actively using it. You can change the schedule time and, as long as the cluster isn’t running, see the dashboard not being able to start the cluster.
item.summary: Dashboards do not run on Schedule when assigned to TerraForm created Compute

comments.comment: Setting to rejected for time being. Schedule seem to be back to normal. Can revisit if issue re-occurs.

These sources have been created as external tables reading from an S3 bucket. This story involves implementing an ingestion pattern with tables that closely match the sources so that downstream gold tables do not pull data directly at the source.

daily production volumes flow.drawio

Out of Scope: Replacing the tables and jobs in the As-Is flow. This work will run in parallel to that.

  3. Bronze tables hold accumulated source data with ingestion time metadata.
  4. Silver tables contain data as it is in the source.

  • Terraform is updated (if applicable)
  • Bronze and Silver source tables exist in Dev and Test
  • Deployment activities are documented in Confluence (if applicable)

item.title: [DF-736] Create SPs to support Workspace API Queries and Admin Deployments
item.description:
I need to define Service Principals to run workspace admin tasks in each workspace, as well as an SP in each workspace that can be provisioned with both “workspace admin” access and API credentials to the Workspace API. This will be used to query the API and can information on workspace configuration and entitlements.

Below is an excerpt from a conversation with Zach:

Scott

Hey, got a question for you:

I have code that uses the Databricks Python SDK to query the Workspace API. In order to that, it defaults to authenticating to the API using the identity of the Service Principal that's running the job; however, I could pass in different credentials (using DB secrets) if I wanted to. Whichever SP I use has to be permissioned with access to the API.

 Do you think it would make more sense to:

  1. Permission each global STL runner SP against the API for their particular workspace
  2. Create a specific SP for each workspace whose credentials I explicitly invoke to query the API
  3. Create a different SP other than the Global STL Runner to run these specific jobs
  4. Something else I haven't thought of

?

Zach

hmm. let me think about that. need to consider where the risk sits in each case under a breach. options 2 and 3 are the same under Keyera's current security requirements.

so its a decision between does the ETL runner SP get access to the API or does a separte SP

Ok so if we are going to follow the general pattern it will be a combination of 1 and 2.

First off there is a different SP runner for every source system. the global one is only used for gold. So you will have a SP Extraction Databricks | <workspace> service principal. That SP then has the ACLs for read access on the secret scope that stores the credentials for accessing the source application. The credentials would then be tied to a different databricks SP.

Now the second SP seems redundant b/c Databricks is the source system in this case, but there is something to be said about sticking to a pattern. It also allows you to manage the 2nd SPs ACLs independently of the runner which is helpful.

All that said, I am still a bit wary of the level of auth being provided to that SP that has access to Databricks. I don't like the idea of it having any broad write style permissions, even on the workspace. Seems risky and would be something that would draw attention in the cyber world if they were to catch wind.

Basically, if that SP has workspace admin, then it can run other jobs and gain access to the secrets that the other SPs have access to.

I'm also curious how you are able to get all the information you need when each SP is only scoped to a single workspace? or are you thinking an job runs in prod but is attached to an SP that has workspace rights on all workspaces?

Scott

Ok, this sounds like a good pattern (if super freakin' involved - lol).

I share your concerns regarding access. I don't think that the SP that queries the API (or, as DB prefers, uses the Python SDK) would need Workspace Admin permissions because it doesn't need to write anything to the API, it just needs to read data.

I haven't found any information on how to set scopes (not Secret Scopes) through either the API or the SDK, so I am thinking that since the SDK authenticates using OAuth, it might restrict access based on what the SP is permissioned on. That said, to list all groups and read their entitlements, maybe that does require Workspace Admin access. I honestly don't know.

Zach

ya permissions will be what the SP has been assigned in that case

it will just depend on the entitlements needed to get that data

Scott

Ok, confirmed. What SP is calling the API needs to be a workspace admin to get the necessary entitlement and membership info.

Zach

hmm. ok. that's not ideal. we will need to review  the data you are trying to access before it leaves PoC and see if there is another way to get you the same information without that level of access.

otherwise we'll get yelled at by cyber security and lose all the good will we have built up over the last year.

Zach

Yeah. It seems like the workspace entitlements data isn't available anywhere else.

So, one thing we could potentially do...I know that the way we have defined "Workspace Admin" groups includes a ton of emergency data access. But this SP doesn't need ANY data access. They just need to be part of the "admins" group for their workspace. Now, that obviously gives them some power, but I don't think that it gives them the ability to do things like create clusters and on it's own it doesn't give them any data access.

It's less privilege than the CI/CD SP, which already has admin rights.

item.title: [DF-722] Restructure Group Entitlements Silver Query
item.description:
I want to restructure the silver query for group entitlements to yield a narrow and long table that I can scan quickly and compare to a known result set.

Here's my final draft SQL query that I want to incorporate into my notebook:

WITH base AS (
SELECT
CAST(`id` AS LONG) AS `id`,
displayName AS `name`,
meta['resourceType'] AS `type`,
CAST(get(groups, 0)['value'] AS LONG) AS `parent_id`,
get(groups, 0)['display'] AS `parent_name`,
e.value AS `entitlement`
FROM
keyera_enterprise_dev.admin.bronze_iam_group_entitlements
LATERAL VIEW OUTER explode(entitlements) AS e
WHERE
get(groups, 0)['value'] IS NULL
UNION
SELECT
CAST(m.value AS LONG) AS `id`,
m.display AS `name`,
`type`,
CAST(id AS LONG) AS `parent_id`,
name AS `parent_name`,
`entitlement`
FROM
(
SELECT
`id`,
displayName AS `name`,
meta['resourceType'] AS `type`,
e.value AS `entitlement`,
members
FROM
keyera_enterprise_dev.admin.bronze_iam_group_entitlements
LATERAL VIEW OUTER explode(entitlements) AS e
) t
LATERAL VIEW OUTER explode(members) AS m
WHERE
m.`$ref` RLIKE 'Groups'
),
admin_ids AS (
SELECT DISTINCT
id
FROM
base
WHERE
name = 'admins'
OR parent_name = 'admins'
),
final_set AS (
SELECT
`id`,
`name`,
`type`,
`parent_id`,
`parent_name`,
`entitlement`
FROM
base
UNION
SELECT
b.id AS `id`,
b.name AS `name`,
b.type AS `type`,
b.parent_id AS `parent_id`,
b.parent_name AS `parent_name`,
'workspace-admin' AS `entitlement`
FROM
base b
JOIN admin_ids a
ON a.id = b.id
)
SELECT
*
FROM
final_set
ORDER BY
`id` ASC
item.summary: Restructure Group Entitlements Silver Query

item.title: [DF-716] Create sample analysis data table
item.description:
Problem:

Currently, the publish_sample_data Glue job exports samples from the MMS database to an S3 table named sample_analysis_data. This job operates on a rolling 30-day window based on the sample's creation date. As a result, any sample created more than 30 days ago is excluded from updates in the S3 table even if it has been modified in MMS.

For accurate reporting, we need to eliminate this 30-day window constraint and present data in a table so that it reflects the current state of all samples in MMS, regardless of their creation date.

item.title: [DF-693] Add Strachan daily mass tag to volumes dashboard (CLC_DAY_MSS_FLO_SUM)
item.description:
Request from Kennedy Gunderson:

I have changed the 'G&P Volumes' query to include the CLC_DAY_MSS_FLO_SUM tag for the production volumes dashboard.

 

I'm not sure if the queries have been changed since we cloned the dashboards to my workspace last, so that might just be something to check for to make sure the query update doesn't delete anything. I'll copy the query here just incase anyone wants to review first!

 

SELECT

    asset_area AS `Asset_Area`,

    prod_date AS `Production Date`,

    parent_q2_device_id AS `Device ID`,

    parent_q2_device_description AS `Device Description`,

    q2_data_tag_description AS `Tag Description`,

    product_code AS `Product Code`,

    q2_data_tag AS `Tag ID`,

    data_tag AS `Data Tag ID`,

    data_value_numeric AS `Value`,

    uom AS `UoM`,

    status as `Status`

FROM keyera_measurement_prod.gold_volumetrics.daily_production_volumes_last_fourteen_months

WHERE asset_area IN ('Brazeau','Keylink','Rimbey','Simonette','Wapiti', 'Strachan')

    AND data_tag IN (

        'PDAY_VOL',

        'PDAY_VOL2',

        'PDAY_VOL_R',

        'CLC_CLINV_VOL',

        'CLC_DAY_MSS_FLO_SUM'

    )

    AND Status != 'Deleted'

ORDER BY asset_area ASC, prod_date DESC, parent_q2_device_id, q2_data_tag
item.summary: Add Strachan daily mass tag to volumes dashboard (CLC_DAY_MSS_FLO_SUM)

item.title: [DF-689] Create Translated Tables
item.description:
MMS tables store database ids, which limits their usefulness for downstream transforms. Downstream tables typically include translated columns that enhance usability. This task aims to create translated versions of MMS tables to streamline and accelerate downstream transformation processes.

Business logic / validations required to QA data? Gladys Salas

Table #1: Product <-> Sample Analysis Group

Catalog: keyera_enterprise_<env>

Schema: gold_measurement

Table name: product_sample_analysis_group_translated

ACL:

  • Read only to: Measurement & Analytics | Consumer | Internal | <Workspace>

Proof of concept table: keyera_measurement_dev.bronze_mms.poc_products

Query:

SELECT *

FROM public.product p

INNER JOIN public.product_sample_analysis_group psag ON p.id = psag.product_id

INNER JOIN public.sample_analysis_group sag ON psag.sample_analysis_group_id = sag.id

  • Description: Relationship table containing products with their corresponding sample analysis group. Include source ids for each derived name.
  • Filters: Only active Sample analysis group records (end_date is null).
  • No auditing required. bronze_mms tables should have historical data.
  • Source tables to join from silver_mms: product, product_sample_analysis_group, sample_analysis_group
    • Include all columns from joined tables.

Table #2: Device <-> Device Type

Catalog: keyera_enterprise_<env>

Schema: gold_measurement

Table name: device_translated

ACL:

  • Read only to: Measurement & Analytics | Consumer | Internal | <Workspace>
  • Description: Device table with translated columns for type and group.
  • No auditing required. bronze_mms tables should have historical data.
  • Source tables to join: device, device_type, device_type_group

Definition of Done

  • Code is Written and Reviewed via Pull Request
  • Code Passes Unit Tests
  • Solution is Documented (README, docstrings, etc.).
  • Terraform is Updated (to create resource dependencies like groups, Service Principals, catalogs, schemas, etc.)
  • Development Deployment is Validated
  • Story is Attached to a Release
  • Release is Deployed to Test

item.summary: MMS Postgres Database Table Ingestion

comments.comment:
Hello, Please find the info requested per table. Let me know if there is anything else required.

1.Device: primary key = id. MMS enforces q2device_id to be unique for a date range delimited by from_date and end_date combination, including no overlaps.

2.Product: primary key = id. MMS enforces q2product_code to be unique.

3.product_sample_analysis_group: primary key = id. Combination of product_id, sample_analysis_group_id and order_of_lookup must be unique.

4.sample_analysis_group: primary key = id. MMS enforces name to be unique.

5.device_type: primary key = id. MMS enforces name to be unique.

6.device_type_group: primary key = id. name to be unique but there is not front end screen in MMS to update the names.

Added tables needed to recreate sample_analysis_data s3 table.

Lee Pattison Gladys Salas

Lee Pattison Pauline Telan Zackary Oleitschuk Polina Pranova

I’ve tested connectivity from our dev-data-extraction workspace (10.180.50.0/23) but had no success connecting to the dev database.

According to Joel, we should have full routing between the AWS Accounts, so probably there is a security rule just blocking the connection.

CC: Melanie Quon
Added subnets for reference
Having connectivity in dev.
Mateo Fidabel are you able to narrow the ip range? Infra / security would like to see if we can reduce exposure in case of a breach.

Oliver Kim Databricks Clusters are provisioned dynamically in AWS, so it is hard to tell from what IP the db connection could be coming from. We could implement some kind of NAT to narrow the IP range to a static one, similar to what Databricks recommends on their docs .

With Pauline Telan we have also considered using Databricks Service Credentials to narrow authentication to only Databricks Data Extraction Clusters instead of anyone with a pair of username/passwd. So even if a malicious request is coming from the subnet, it won’t be able to authenticate against the database. But we have noticed that this feature is turned off in MMS databases.

CC: Zackary Oleitschuk

item.title: [DF-678] Maximo DATETIME fields are nontimezone where databricks DATETIMEOFFSET incl timezone
item.description:
ISSUE:

Maximo datetime (well any SQL database) has no timezone info. 

2024-11-29 13:01:56.180

Databricks is presenting datetimeoffset with timezone – currently the +0:00 would be inccorect representation of the same record

2024-11-29T13:01:56.180+00:00

POSSIBLE SOLUTIONS:

  • in databricks store it as the same datatype, datetime (no timezone)
    • 2024-11-29 13:01:56.180
    • PRO: ez to use its cgy time
    • CON:
  • in databricks convert the maximo (sql) datetime to datetimeoffset for example with UTC-7:00
    • 2024-11-29T04:01:56.180-07:00
    • PRO:
    • CON: when using this datetime, its annoying to convert to local time.
  • any others Zackary Oleitschuk ? does/can

DECISION: Oliver Kim Zackary Oleitschuk Lee Pattison

Votes:

Final Answer:

Timestamp formats in Databricks - Data Foundations - Confluence
item.summary: Maximo DATETIME fields are nontimezone where databricks DATETIMEOFFSET incl timezone

comments.comment:
UTC-7 is more correct, OTOH if the keyera standard has always been calgary time, we can just use the simplest solution until we have to fix.

Is there any concern with plains acquisition and merging data / timezones? Any other possible data warehouse type of problems like syncing dates with S2P and other SaaS products… might be better to convert to UTC offset as a rule…

Oliver Kim I think because of the acquisition we probably have to store timezone info. It’s also worth noting that plant and pipeline time are different than standard timezones, in that I believe they ignore daylight saving time.

Jonathan Yun My vote is for: “In databricks store it as the same datatype, datetime (no timezone)”

Rationale: This is a bronze table, so should be identical to source. Changing it at this stage may also impact de-duplication in the silver table.

If we need to have a date with an offset, I’d think it would be better to do that in a gold table. At that point, maybe you have two date columns, one as the original, and one with the offset applied.

when we (maximo) send/integrate dates to welltrak for example, we get the ‘local time as stored in system/db', convert to utc with timezone info and send to welltrak webservice who receives it as utc but converts it to their local db time to write to the DB with no timezone info.

maximo keeps the ‘server/db timezone’. the ui applies the persons timezone in code

i dont know what the other systems use/have

thanks lee, i also agree, in databricks store it as the same datatype, datetime (no timezone)

is this a this sprint fix or next

I’ve deleted some comments they may mislead future readers. We are storing dates as timestamps, which store fields year, month, day, hour, minute, second, and local timezone.

https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/sql/language-manual/data-types/timestamp-typehttps://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/sql/language-manual/data-types/timestamp-type

The documentation states that dates will be converted to utc prior to storage (see notes) so I think if we store without manipulation, then extract without supplying a timezone, there will be confusion in the future as developers assume the timezone is utc…

so based on comments floating around outside of jira, we still have 2 options:

  1. Store as a plain timestamp the same way it is stored in the source database, leave timezone conversion for later, probably when converting from bronze to silver.
  2. Discover source timezone at extraction, code it into the extraction, and store as timestamp with local timezone (which will normalize to utc when stored in databricks).

I favor option 2 as you are dealing with something that is known at extraction time, but happy to consider alternatives, especially if we’re already doing things a certain way in existing extractions.

Discussion with df architecture team - decision is to use unadulterated timestamp type without timezone information and handle conversions / normalization at GOLD layer…. Oliver will document in confluence.

item.title: [DF-663] Duplicates in gold_volumetrics.daily_production_volumes_last_14_days
item.description:
Kennedy reported duplicates in the production gold_volumetrics.daily_production_volumes_last_14_days table.

From Kennedy:

I've noticed there are many duplicates occurring in the production daily volumes table. We have corrected any duplicate data from MMS at the source by deleting duplicate entries. These should be left out in the daily production volumes dashboard since we don't include any 'deleted' records there. However, I am wondering if there is a transformation step that is causing an amplification of duplicates between the final measurement data table and the daily production volume - last 14 months table.  For example, we have a duplicate KFS_FQ_115.PDAY_MSS record on 2025-07-10 appearing 8 times, and they all have a status of 'Validated-System'. These duplicates do not appear in any other table/AWS bucket or in MMS, as far as I have found.  If you have the time to look into why we are getting so many duplicates that would be fantastic.
item.summary: Duplicates in gold_volumetrics.daily_production_volumes_last_14_days

comments.comment:
�� Hi Mateo Fidabel can I ask for your help on this please? Been a bit stomped.. I suspect that this is a scd2 bug because the issue doesn’t seem to happen for all records, only some.

Attached is a list of the duplicates I got from silver Test and Prod + the query I used to get the duplicates.

SELECT *
FROM silver_volumetrics.daily_production_volumes
WHERE end_date IS NULL
  AND (prod_date, q2_data_tag, status) IN (
    SELECT prod_date, q2_data_tag, status
    FROM silver_volumetrics.daily_production_volumes
    WHERE end_date IS NULL
    GROUP BY prod_date, q2_data_tag, status
    HAVING COUNT(*) > 1
  )
  ORDER BY prod_date, q2_data_tag

duplicates.xlsx

Observations so far:

  • The duplicates exist in both silver_volumetrics.daily_production_volumes and gold_volumetrics.daily_production_volumes_last_14_days
  • Duplicates seem to have started appearing around July 20
  • Duplicates exist in Dev, Test, Prod (edit: added Dev)

If you want to pull the code please take it from the release/1.0.0 branch in the keyera-databricks-measurements repo. The job running in Test is using the Measurements bundle version.

gold_volumetrics.daily_production_volumes_last_14_days is not an SCD2 table so I believe calling results_df = results_df.DropDuplicates() before writing to the table should be sufficient to ensure there are no duplicates in gold. This patch will be included in{{release/1.0.0}} of the measurements bundle.

While this change should fix gold, there is still an issue with the SCD2 merge utility since it inserts duplicates in silver (e.g. KFS_FQ_115.PDAY_MSS on 2025-07-10 has multiple end_date = null entries with the same effective_date).

Created new Jira to track the silver SCD2 bug. https://keyera.atlassian.net/browse/DF-703

We have project management metadata in an Excel file (Requests and Data Products Inventory.xlsx) stored on the project SharePoint site. We also have exported Jira data that track project work. A fully automated ingestion pipeline may not be required as these tables are likely to be replaced by internally managed data sources in future. However, to prototype processes and provide project dashboards, we need to ingest the Excel data. This can be done by uploading the files to a dedicated volume and running a notebook to ingest the files.

This also has two secondary benefits:

  2. Expected reuse of a general purpose Excel file ingestion notebook for ad hoc work.

item.title: [DF-656] Databricks Platform Administration
item.description:
Stories and tasks related to platform administration, auditing, etc.

Platform Administration Items

  • Complete implementation of Terraform for IaC (Infrastructure-as-Code) deployment
    • Terraform is used with Databricks to define and deploy our workspaces, data catalogs, business domain data schemas, primary service principals, groups, all-purpose compute, compute policies, SQL warehouses, and to apply security permissions to all of the above.
  • Transition AWS Configuration to Terraform
    • Similar to Databricks, Terraform can be used with AWS to define and deploy resources as IaC. We should be using this to deploy the underlying S3 storage, virtual private clusters, and virtual private network assets for our Databricks environments.
  • IAM Validation
    • Databricks includes the ability to define groups, users, and service principals with fine-grained access permissions. However, it lacks built-in tools to effectively manage these objects and permissions,
    • This is a collection of notebooks, jobs, tables, and dashboards intended to validate that our system’s groups, users, and service principals, and their associated security permissions, conform to our expected state (as defined in the Terraform above). These will allow us to 1. validate that the Terraform configuration is correct, 2. detect whether any changes have been made since a Terraform deployment (either by jobs or manually), and 3. maintain a history of our IAM posture, which will improve our ability to audit access and investigate any issues.
  • Auditing Scripts
    • Databricks includes robust logging of almost all system events and writes those logs to system tables. However, it does not have built-in tools to analyze those logs and surface potentially concerning items. It also does not maintain this history for more than 1 year.
    • This will be a library of scripts that will define potentially concerning activity, parse the system logs, and flag any items that we specify. We can also use this code base to store relevant audit logs within our own AWS storage, ensuring that we meet Keyera’s data retention policies.
  • Implement DR, Backup, and Archival Patterns
    • We need to define and implement our disaster recovery, source data backup, and result data archival patterns.
    • This needs to include DR plans for IaC code, ETL code, virtual infrastructure fail-over, and backup of S3.
  • Unification of Ingestion Patterns (potential)
    • We currently use multiple patterns for ingestion of data from source systems (e.g., SQL CDC, DMS CDC, direct query, API query). This is not necessarily an issue and is – to some extent – unavoidable. However, it does increase complexity and may also increase costs. We should consider future work to normalize our ingestion patterns, where and when it makes sense.
  • Decommissioning of Commercial Solutions Workspaces
    • The Commercial Solutions workspaces were created as part of a separate Databricks pilot conducted with Arcurve. It has always been the plan to decommission these workspaces and merge their content into the Data Extraction and Analytics Lakehouse workspaces. This will free up workspace quota, reduce cost, and dramatically simplify system management.
  • Integration of all ETL into Primary Code Base
    • At present there are multiple distinct code bases handling ETL tasks: keyera-databricks, keyera-emissions, keyera-measurement, and (to a lesser extent) databricks-admin. We should consolidate all ETL code into a single code base to improve maintainability, transparency, and control.
  • Configuration of Power BI as Presentation Layer
    • We need to more fully investigate and possibly configure Power BI since the business uses it as their preferred presentation layer.
  • Implementation of Automated Code Documentation
    • Our code is documented with docstrings and readme files. We should investigate and implement an automated documentation system to consolidate and publish this technical documentation.
item.summary: Databricks Platform Administration

item.title: [DF-618] Maximo - Promote PO + POLINE tables from silver to production w/restricted/pii
item.description:
PURPOSE: this epic is to ensure the PO and POLINE tables are either restricted or scrubbed or filtered at the catalog silver or gold level

HIGH LEVEL: unsure if we use the post refresh or we replicate the maximo “global data restrictions” be user group – assume anything restricted is restricted

2025sept15:

  • zack advised we would do a meterialized view on the table then add a column mask using below rules provided at the gold level
  • we will have to create groups in databricks based on the security/user/person groups in maximo

–

PO + POLINE tables moved to dbk bronze + silver in DF-61 Deploy

silver level data needs to be restricted/masked

original design was to use sql (enterprise) masking or sql (enterprise) row level security but as we are now using DataBricks as the warehouse, we will apply the security levels at databricks Silver and Gold level tables for permissioning to users

code snippet – was designed to set to $1 in DEV env refreshes. includes other tables as well like invoice/receipts

/* scrub SCM RESTRICTED records --> set to 1.0
contract/pr/prline/po/poline/receipts/invoice/invoiceline records 
*************************************************************************/
if ( @pSCRUBRESTRICT = 'Y' )
begin

update contract set totalcost=1,totalbasecost=1, key_parta='##KEY_RESTRICT##', key_partb='##KEY_RESTRICT##',key_partc='##KEY_RESTRICT##',key_partd='##KEY_RESTRICT##',revcomments='##KEY_RESTRICT##'
-- select totalcost,totalbasecost,key_parta,key_partb,key_partc,key_partd,* from contract 
where key_restrict is not null 

update contractline set orderqty =1, unitcost=1, linecost=1
-- select * from contractline 
where contractnum in (select distinct contractnum from contract where key_restrict is not null )

update pr set totalcost =1, totaltax1=1,key_prevappr=null, key_parta='##KEY_RESTRICT##', key_partb='##KEY_RESTRICT##',key_partc='##KEY_RESTRICT##',key_partd='##KEY_RESTRICT##'
-- select * from pr 
where key_restrict is not null 
	or	
	contractrefnum in (select distinct contractnum from contract where key_restrict is not null)

update prline set orderqty=1, unitcost=1, linecost=1, tax1=1,loadedcost=1,linecost1=1, loadedcost1=1
-- select * from prline 
where prnum in (select distinct prnum from pr where key_restrict is not null)
	or	contractrefnum in (select distinct contractnum from contract where key_restrict is not null)

-- STAGE POLIST FOR SCRUBBING -- NOTE: siteless because easier
select ponum, revisionnum, siteid, totalcost, totaltax1, poid
into #key_restrict_polist
from po 
where key_restrict is not null
	or	
	contractrefnum in (select distinct contractnum from contract where key_restrict is not null)

update po set totalcost=1, totaltax1=1,key_cascarvalue=null, key_parta='##KEY_RESTRICT##', key_partb='##KEY_RESTRICT##',key_partc='##KEY_RESTRICT##',key_partd='##KEY_RESTRICT##',revcomments='##KEY_RESTRICT##'
--select ponum,revisionnum, totalcost, totaltax1, * from po 
where ponum in (select distinct ponum from #key_restrict_polist)

update poline set orderqty=1, unitcost=1, receivedunitcost=1, receivedqty=1, receivedtotalcost=1, linecost=1, loadedcost=1, tax1=1, linecost1=1, loadedcost1=1 , description = '##KEY_RESTRICT##'
--  select orderqty, unitcost, receivedunitcost, receivedtotalcost, linecost, tax1, loadedcost, linecost1, loadedcost1, loadedcost, * from poline 
where ponum in (select distinct ponum from #key_restrict_polist)

update pocost set linecost=1, loadedcost=1, quantity=1
-- select linecost, loadedcost, quantity, * from pocost
where ponum in (select distinct ponum from #key_restrict_polist)

update matrectrans set quantity = 1, unitcost=1,actualcost=1,linecost=1, currencylinecost=1,currencyunitcost=1,loadedcost=1,tax1=1,qtyrequested=1,linecost2=1
-- select * from matrectrans 
where ponum in (select distinct ponum from #key_restrict_polist)

update servrectrans set rejectqty =0, quantity=1, linecost=1,currencyunitcost=1, currencylinecost=iif(currencylinecost<0, -1,1), loadedcost=1, tax1=1
-- select * from servrectrans 
where ponum in (select distinct ponum from #key_restrict_polist)

update matusetrans set quantity=iif(quantity<0, -1,1), unitcost=1, actualcost=1,linecost=1, currencyunitcost=1, qtyrequested=1, linecost2=1
-- select * from matusetrans 
where ponum in --(select distinct ponum from po where key_restrict is not null)
	(select distinct ponum from po where key_restrict is not null
		or	
	contractrefnum in (select distinct contractnum from contract where key_restrict is not null)
	)

update invoice set totaltax1=1, totalcost=1, basetotalcost=1
-- select totaltax1, totalcost, basetotalcost,* from invoice 
where ponum in (select distinct ponum from #key_restrict_polist)

update invoiceline set invoiceqty=1, linecost=1, tax1=1, loadedcost=1
-- select invoiceqty, linecost, tax1, loadedcost, * from invoiceline 
where ponum in (select distinct ponum from #key_restrict_polist)

update invoicematch set quantity=1, linecost=1
-- select * from invoicematch 
where ponum in (select distinct ponum from #key_restrict_polist)

update invoicecost set unitcost=1, linecost=1,quantity=1
-- select * from invoicecost
where invoicenum in (
	select distinct invoicenum from invoice where ponum in (select distinct ponum from #key_restrict_polist)
		--where ponum in (select distinct ponum from po where key_restrict is not null) 
	union all
	select distinct invoicenum from invoiceline where ponum in (select distinct ponum from #key_restrict_polist)
	)

item.title: [DF-610] Migrate CI/CD pipelines to use OIDC
item.description:
Our Databricks pipelines currently use service principal client secrets for Databricks CLI authentication. These secrets expire every year so these need to be manually generated from Databricks and updated in Bitbucket.

This story involves updating the pipelines to use OIDC which automates token generation: [Enable workload identity federation for Terraform Cloud, Bitbucket Pipelines, or Jenkins - Azure Databricks | Microsoft Learn|https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/databricks/dev-tools/auth/provider-other#atlassian-bitbucket-pipelines].
item.summary: Migrate CI/CD pipelines to use OIDC

item.title: [DF-609] Composition Data and Flow Weighted Average for Any MMS meter
item.description:
The Measurement team has requested the ability to produce the Monthly Composition of the Product measured by a given meter and also to produce the Monthly Flow Weighted Average.

MMS currently calculates the Composition for meters that are configured in Balance Groups but not all meters in the system are included in one or more Balance Groups. Therefore, the calculation needs to be performed using different inputs than Balance Configuration.

Gold Table Specifications

Measurement: Monthly Flow-Weighted Average - Data Foundations - Confluence

Measurement: Daily Flow-Weighted Average Volumes - Data Foundations - Confluence

Acceptance Criteria

  • MMS tables required exist in Databricks
  • Gold Table(s) created as per specifications
  • Gold Table Metadata - Table is tagged with metadata, table and column descriptions loaded into Databricks
  • Access provisioned to tables as per requirements
  • Monthly Flow weighted avg PowerBI report is created

Definition of Done

  • All DoD Criteria for associated user stories and tasks have been completed and signed off.
  • Business UAT Completed
  • Business Sign-off received
item.summary: Composition Data and Flow Weighted Average for Any MMS meter

comments.comment: To be able to provide the functionality requested, MMS needs an enhancement that is being estimated by Arcurve as of 20250716: https://keyera.atlassian.net/browse/QAW-746
Output table definitions (WIP) : DF-609 - Flow Weighted Volumes.xlsx

As per discussions with Tania Nezic on 20250711 and 20250714, these are the high level requirements to provide the Composition and Flow Weighted Average in Databricks. Note: This functionality will also be used for WADF calculations (requirements provided by Bill Wells).

As per our discussions, we are designing for the following high level requirements:

  1. (Bill Wells request) The C7+ composition for liquid meters is calculated using different inputs than in the MMS Balance (C7+ Density and Molar Mass in Sample Analysis in effect).  Therefore, results will be slightly different between FWA calculation and the MMS Balance.
  2. Device Type in scope: Meters
  3. Devices in scope: Meters with associated Default Sample Point (jira 746 in MMS project)
  4. Tags in scope: Tags with .PDAY_VOL suffix
  5. Products in scope: Products configured in MMS with at least one Analysis Group for Component Balancing value
  6. Search parameters requested: Asset Area, Parent Q2 Device Id, Device Description, Product, Month-Year(s)

item.description:
do we exclude/filter out the data before databricks ingestion

or do we apply role and row level (or field level) security in databricks.

for example, PO table will include the committed cost for Stoic. long description will contain rates. attachements will contain agreed contract. receipts and invoices in maximo (and qbyte) will have the invoice costs.

discussion points:

  • originally, we were going to implement sql server data masking and/or row level security as we have SQL Server Enterprise
  • in non-prod environments, we set the dollar amounts to $1. we can re-use this in databricks to define the tables and columns that require masking

booked meeting monday 2pm with Virmesh and Marco to confirm:

  • Confirming we are using replication for Maximo.
  • we should promote Welltrak replication as well.  
  • do we have a PRODUCTION replication server to put maximo-sub to?   should we use DBP033 or is there security risk with the linked servers access.  new server?
  • NOTE: Joel advised we do NOT want to use the livesync DR servers.  it is for DR only.
    • do we want to use commvault cloning/replication instead using the backups?  https://documentation.commvault.com/v11/essential/creating_instant_clone_for_sql_server.html
  • how do you want me to secure confidential data when replicated to databricks?  do we EXCLUDE ?  do we trust databricks will apply the correct security
    • how do i show this to an auditor?

item.title: [DF-600] OS BD & Logistics (eONE & Qbyte)
item.description:
OS BD

Background

OS BD Team requires an all-encompassing report that summarizes its performance in relation to customers volume with the FSCS product system. The OS BD team requires eONE data to:

  1. Track customer volumes and revenue to improve strategy/commercial relations
  2. Prepare annual budgets, 5-year forecasts, expected volumes, expected revenues
  3. Access/visibility to daily volumetric data to track production against the budget/plan 

Request

Data examples are stored in the ‘Oilsands Data Integration Breakdown’ shared with Melanie, Gladys, and Lee. Data table requests listed by priority and accessibility: 

eONE:

  1. ‘Keyera Account Journal Qbyte Detail’ ingestion – this report provides key financial information based on the contracted volumes OS customers are receiving monthly. The table also has key columns (Resp cost Center Qbyte) to connect eONE data to the Qbyte system, allowing an in-depth analysis on asset performance margins.
  2. ‘Product Inventory” Workflow ingestion – provides further breakdown on the customer contracts, providing nuances to each individual contract additional fees or make up rights that is not represented in the rolled-up Account Journal. Key items provide OS BD with intel on opportunities to increase fees, improving revenue.
  3. ‘C5 Daily Balance’ (unable to source as it sits on the logistics side) - is an excel logistics manually fills in and inputs into eONE with volumes by customer by receipt/delivery point. This data would be the key for strategic planning as it will provide BD with knowledge of the upstream supply Keyera is currently capturing (market capture).  

Definition of Done 

  • Quality volume and financial data from eONE, Qbyte and MMs/QQ 
  • Be able to identify but not limited to the 14 receipt points and 7 delivery points in eONE and MMs/QQ (MMS 75% verified) 
  • Validate customer specific data including volumes flowing through each receipt/delivery point (eONE from the logistics side) 
  • QA/QC with accounting reports 
  • Access to the required data to prepare: 
    • Power Bi dashboard – includes identification of volume flows by customer, revenue by customer and OPEX  
    • Annual budgets 
    • Gross OPEX 
    • Operating Margin 
    • 5 year forecast 
    • Expected volumes 
    • Expected costs (by month) 
    • Capital project costs 
    • Ability to measure monthly customer volumes  
    • Report on profit vs. spend 
    • Ability to link volume flow to contract fee for Keyera Corp. 

Data Products

  1. Summarized Operations Data Extract 
  2. LI Customer Operations 
  3. KPLI – Keyera Account Journal QByte Detail report

Logistics

Background

The Logistics team currently uses a Power BI report called “Daily Facility Balance” to monitor daily storage volumes by commodity and customer. The current process for data ingestion is a three-step workflow: 

  1. Schedulers manually input the data into eOne. 
  2. IT has set up an automated export of the eOne report, which is sent to the Logistics service account mailbox in CSV format. 
  3. A Power Automate flow uploads the CSV to a SharePoint folder, from which Power BI pulls the data. 

While functional, this process is manual and prone to delay. We're now looking to leverage Databricks to streamline data access and automate the flow of KFS Frac & Storage Facility volumetric data into a historical dataset. The goal is to create a more efficient, scalable, and automated reporting pipeline.

Request

Please refer to the attached file: “Previous Two Month – Facility Balance Detail.” 

  • eOne Data Access: We have an existing eOne report set up, though the exact report name is still TBD.
  • Data Scope Request: Currently, we only receive data for the previous two months, which we then manually merge with historical records. We’re requesting access to a complete master table that includes all past days’ data, starting from September 2024. This would eliminate manual merging and ensure full historical visibility in Power BI.

Definition of Done

  • We have full access to historical data going back to September 2024. 
  • Quality metrics are accurate by owner, counterparty, and location. These will be validated with the rail and truck teams once the data is complete. 
  • Power BI is successfully connected to the data source. 
  • Data is refreshed daily (with a one-day lag) and is available by 10 AM each day.

item.description:
The latest knowledge base documents and metadata need to be deployed to PROD.

They can be found in the Bitbucket repository in the folder:

backend > knowledge_bases > benny

they can be deployed with the upload-docs.sh command
(first, install and configure WSL, instructions here: https://bitbucket.org/keyeradataservices/keyera-genai-bedrock-chatbot/src/main/DEVELOPMENT_SETUP.md )

source config/prod_env
aws sso login
cd backend/knowledge_bases/benny
./upload-docs.sh hr_docs prod

That uploads the documents to the S3 bucket.

Then, you’ll need to login to the AWS Console and sync the knowledge base itself.

item.title: [DF-584] Rail Logistics
item.description:
Product Description
Agent A list of parties, including their addresses, involved in a rail shipments - customers, consignees, care-of, importers, exporters, freight payors, customs payors, customs brokers, etc.
Sequence A list of contracts between Keyra and Customers for rail shipments. Only Propane contracts included. The list in Geo is sourced from eOne deals.
Route A list of routes available to use for rail shipments orders. A route for rail shipments is a data structure that includes essential details about product movement, such as origin, destination, railroads and junctions, product, consignee, freight payment terms, and payors.
Order A list of orders for product movement. An order is a request for specific product movement, detailing the loading month, number of railcars, shipper, product, facility, route, and additional parties of interest (such as care of, importer, exporter, customs broker, payor, notify party). It also includes contracts, export permits, embargo information, instructions for facilities, and Order Status
Order Detail A list of shipments for each order. A shipment is a record creted in Geo for each car on the Order. Each Order Detail contains information about shipments dates (planned, scheduled, shipped), shipment status, physical railcar assigned, name of BOL file generated for the shipment
BOL Bill of Lading documents in pdf format for cars shipped
item.summary: Rail Logistics

item.description:
This Jira ticket is created for getting the data from Databricks dashboard from Measurement: Production Volumes Databricks Dashboard to Excel for the end user. Following Wallena Kendericks's request that all front-end data be accessed digitally—similar to how KFS front-end is connected to their DCS/Historian—we have a new ask to ensure that front-end users no longer need to manually upload or download data from Databricks. This initiative is designed to streamline daily accounting, BD, and logistics processes by integrating the necessary data directly into Excel. item.title: [DF-545] Gold 8: G&P BD - Customer Volume Projections table
item.description:
As a BD rep, I need to estimate allocated customer inlet volumes and NGL components based on historical TIPS values and to-date volumes.

Business context: There is up to 6-week lag in posting TIPS monthly volumes. During that time, BDs have limited visibility into facility operation and customer activity. This data can be estimated using historical data from TIPS, together with up-to-date daily data from Measurements (with GEF (Gas Equivalent Factor) applied to liquid volumes).

Technical Details:

The data must be presented to the business in the following columns:

# Name Description and logic
1 plant_no Unique plant_no from Posted Volumes.
For the purpose of this story, apply filters to limit the data to SIMPT and WAPTT only.
2 Projection From Date
  1. In the Posted Volumes table, for that plant_no (column 1), find the latest production month (PROD_DT).
  2. Set the Projection From Date to be the 1st of the month after the latest production month.
3 Projection To Date Current date - 1 day.
4 meter_no All unique combinations of plant_no, meter_no, ctr_party_ba_no, ba_nm1, and of the latest combination of accounting_date and production_date from Posted Volumes.
5 ctr_party_ba_no All unique combinations of plant_no, meter_no, ctr_party_ba_no, ba_nm1, and of the latest combination of accounting_date and production_date from Posted Volumes.
6 BA_NM1 All unique combinations of plant_no, meter_no, ctr_party_ba_no, ba_nm1, and of the latest combination of accounting_date and production_date from Posted Volumes.
7 q2_tag_id For meter_no (column 4), in the tips_q2_meter_mapping, find the Q2 tag ID for that meter.
8 MTD_INLET_VOLUME For the Q2_tag, in gold_volumetrics.daily_flow_weighted_volumes, add up all volume_m3 values for a time period between Projection From and Projection To dates.
9 CUSTOMER_SHARE_PRIOR_1_PERIOD For ctr_party_ba_no and meter_no, in keyera_enterprise_prod.gold_tips.customer_volume_historical_proportions, find customer_share_of_inlet_percent.
10 MTD_INLET_CUSTOMER_VOLUME Multiply MTD_INLET_VOLUME*CUSTOMER_SHARE_PRIOR_1_PERIOD.
11 CUSTOMER_SHARE_C2_PRIOR_1_PERIOD For a ctr_party_ba_no and meter_no, in keyera_enterprise_prod.gold_tips.customer_volume_historical_proportions, find ethane_c2_yield_percent.
12 ETHANE_C2_VOL_PROJ_PRIOR_1_PERIOD
  1. For the Q2_tag, in gold_volumetrics.daily_flow_weighted_volumes, add up all the values of c2_vol_e3m3 column for a time period between Projection From and Projection To dates.
  2. Multiply the calculated sum by the CUSTOMER_SHARE_PERCENT_PRIOR_1_PERIOD.
13 CUSTOMER_SHARE_C3_PRIOR_1_PERIOD  
14 ETHANE_C3_VOL_PROJ_PRIOR_1_PERIOD  
15    
16    
17    
     

If there is a new customer or a new meter since volume posting, there will be no visibility and the data will be inaccurate.

To make a projection till ME, we need to divide the MTD volume by number of days, determine daily average and then multiply by the number of days in the month.

See full description in the metadata file (link).

See calculations in the model file (link).

Update frequency - daily
item.summary: Gold 8: G&P BD - Customer Volume Projections table

item.title: [DF-509] Create Data Transformation Pipeline
item.description:
Transformation takes cleaned data from silver tables and applies business logic and joins to produce gold tables. This work is expected to require a high degree of domain knowledge and data analysis effort.

Please provide a description of the transformation workflow(s) required, including the input silver tables and expected output of gold tables. If the Data Product requires more than one transformation workflow or requires complex transformation, we may need to create more than one story. Use the questions below to guide your work.

  • How will the data be used (e.g., internal analysis, machine learning, presentation to end users)?
  • What is the shape of the source data and what shape is needed in the final product?
  • Does the data need to be normalized or joined with other data sets to be useful?
  • Is the source data already well understood, or does it require additional exploration and manipulation by a data analyst?
item.summary: Create Data Transformation Pipeline

item.title: [DF-508] Ingest Data from Source System
item.description:
Ingestion covers connecting to source systems, creating bronze tables and extracting data into those tables, cleaning the data, and loading it into silver tables. Note: It does not include the application of business logic or the creation of gold tables.

Please provide a description of the source systems and the tables that will be ingested, along with any technical requirements. If the Data Product requires more than one source system or requires multiple steps to connect and stage the data, we may need to create more than one story. Use the questions below to guide your work.

  • What source systems are we ingesting from?
  • What method are we using to connect to those systems?
  • Are the data sources relatively easy to access or do they require extra development to connect (e.g., is it an internal system with an accessible database, does it have an object model that makes it difficult to query, do we need to pull the data from an API and do we have access)?
  • What is the necessary refresh cadence?
  • What is the desired ingest granularity?
  • What is the structure of the source system data?
  • Are there data quality considerations that need to be overcome?
  • What are the characteristics of the source data that we need to be aware of (e.g., refresh cadence, quality, granularity)?
  • How clean is the source data and does it conform to Keyera standards (e.g., quality, units of measure)?
item.summary: Ingest Data from Source System

item.title: [DF-486] Ingest "Raw" Measurement Data from AWS
item.description:
Objective

Enable business users to access unvalidated, raw production volume data earlier in the day so they can begin working with it before MMS validation is complete. This is achieved by enhancing the existing gold_volumetrics.daily_production_volumes_last_fourteen_months table and introducing a supporting pipeline that stages and updates tag data progressively.

Step 0: Create External Table Over AWS S3

  • Define an external table named bronze_q2.inmation_raw_measurement_data.
  • Point it directly to the AWS S3 bucket in the Q2 account where raw measurement data is stored.
  • Avoid any transformations at this stage — the table should reflect the raw schema and structure of the source files.
  • Ensure the table includes a data_load_time column to support downstream filtering.

Step 1: Build silver_volumetrics.unvalidated_last_2_days

  • Create a new table or view named silver_volumetrics.unvalidated_last_2_days.
  • Source data from bronze_q2.inmation_raw_measurement_data.
  • Apply a filter: prod_date >= current_date - 2.
  • Add a derived column status:
    • Set status = "UNVALIDATED" for all records.
  • This table will serve as the authoritative source for recent unvalidated tag data and will be used in downstream logic.

Step 2: Modify gold_volumetrics.daily_production_volumes_last_fourteen_months

  • Update the logic of this existing table to incorporate tag data from:
    • silver_volumetrics.unvalidated_last_2_days for recent unvalidated tags.
    • silver_volumetrics.daily_production_volumes for MMS-validated tags.
  • Tag Source Logic by Production Date:
    • For {{prod_date = current_date - 2}}and beyond:
      • Use MMS data from silver_volumetrics.daily_production_volumes.
      • Use the status value provided by MMS (e.g., "Validated-System/Reviewed/etc").
    • For prod_date = current_date - 1:
      • Use tag data from silver_volumetrics.unvalidated_last_2_days.
      • Use the status column already assigned in Step 1 ("UNVALIDATED").
      • If there is a validated volume from MMS from that tag, take the MMS volume over the unvalidated tag volume.

Step 3: Update Existing Job

  • Modify the existing Databricks job named Daily Production Volumes to:
    • Include logic for ingesting and processing data from silver_volumetrics.unvalidated_last_7_days.
    • Run every 15 minutes between 07:00 and 09:00 local time.
    • Update gold_volumetrics.daily_production_volumes_last_fourteen_months with the latest tag data and statuses.
item.summary: Ingest "Raw" Measurement Data from AWS

item.title: [DF-483] Measurement Data
item.description:
• Business Owner: Tyson van Leusden
  • Business Lead: Tania Nezic

Why

What is the business problem that we are trying to solve with data?

A “data product” is a package of work that results in one or more related data sets that are available to data analysts and/or business consumers. Most often, a data product will require work related to definition, ingestion, transformation, processing, and consumption.

Rather than being defined by tables in a source system, data products should be defined by deliverables that are tied to some business capability. For example:

�� “I want the data from 13 tables in Qbyte so that I can query the data for my report.”

“I want to create a dashboard for our PMO, to support our Source-to-Pay effort by showing how cloud infrastructure costs relate to our project portfolio.”

What is the value of solving this problem?

What is the value of solving the problem? Wherever possible, provide a statement of tangible and quantifiable business value.

  • Allows for joining measurement data to other data sets for wider usage.
  • Combines measurement data with business context.
  • Publishes measurement data to wider audiences.

What is/isn’t the urgency tied to solving this problem?

Volumetric data is fundamental to all business lines and to enabling our analysts.

How

How will we solve this problem with data?

  • We need to provide timely access to a variety of measurement data sets, especially:
    • Volumes
    • Compositions
    • Balancing
    • Sensor Calibrations (WellTrak)
  • In addition to the raw datasets, we will also make broad data available through Databricks Dashboards and via Power BI semantic models.

What

What are the specific deliverables? See the “Define” story for more on capturing requirements.

  1. Delivery of “raw” volume data - incorporate previous day PDAY (production day) tagged data from AWS MMS Raw data store to enable the use of daily data in nominations processes.
    1. Incorporation of the raw data into the Production Volumes Databricks Dashboard
    2. Replacement of raw data with validated data once available
  2. Access to balance data - so that we can streamline (and not recalculate) providing balance group data and flow weighted average sample date. (60 Day history - verify Pauline Telan)
  3. Delivery of curated volume data tables - the existing “gold_volumetrics” tables are too large and have variable granularity (minute, hour, day data is mixed). We must undertake data analysis and determine a set of more curated gold tables to increase usability.
  4. Other Compositional Data - for Measurement Quality Team Reporting & Logistics use. Includes:
    1. KeyeraC5+Eq
    2. KeyeraTraceSulphur
    3. KeyeraOther (Deana/Teresa)
  5. Access to WellTrak Data
  6. Translate the queries behind the Measurements Dashboard into gold tables so the curated data can be used by PA and other audiences.
  7. Ingest relational information (e.g., meter and sample point) from MMS PostgreSQL database.
  8. Possibly create component balancing table POC in sandbox - Bill Wells

item.title: [DF-448] FR-14 DUC+ to FreshService integration will include process to add, update, or remove SCIs (may be automated or manual)
item.description:
DESCRIPTION
Create process documentation to facilitate the integration to support the addition, update, and removal of SCIs (Service Catalog Items). This process may be automated or manual depending on the scope and complexity of the task. I would suggest we focus on manual process and convert that to an automated process should we have the resources to do so. The goal is to ensure accurate and timely synchronization of SCI data between DUC+ and FreshService to support service management workflows.

This enhancement improves data consistency and operational efficiency in configuration management.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA

  • The integration process supports adding, updating, and removing SCIs in FreshService based on the content of the DUC+.
  • Manual and automated processes are clearly defined and documented.
  • SCI changes are logged and auditable.

OUT OF SCOPE

  • SCI management for systems not tracked in DUC+.
  • Enhancements to DUC+ or FreshService outside of SCI synchronization.

DEPENDENCIES

  • API or data access to DUC+ and FreshService.
  • Defined SCI data model and mapping rules.
  • Authentication and authorization for integration endpoints.

NOTES

  • Ensure compliance with Keyera’s configuration management and audit policies.
  • Include error handling and alerting for failed sync operations.
  • This enhancement lays the groundwork for broader CMDB automation.
item.summary: FR-14 DUC+ to FreshService integration will include process to add, update, or remove SCIs (may be automated or manual)

item.title: [DF-447] FR-13 Orchestration Server will run scripts that configure access to approved security groups
item.description:
DESCRIPTION
Enhance the Orchestration Server to execute scripts that configure access to approved security groups. These scripts will be triggered by upstream workflow approvals (e.g., from FreshService) and will automate the provisioning of access entitlements based on predefined rules and mappings.

This enhancement supports scalable, policy-driven access management and reduces manual effort in provisioning tasks.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA

  • The Orchestration Server can execute scripts that apply access configurations to security groups.
  • Scripts are parameterized and support logging, error handling, and rollback where applicable.
  • Scripts should be version controlled.

OUT OF SCOPE

  • Manual access provisioning or approval workflows.
  • Integration with systems not included in the approved access scope.

DEPENDENCIES

  • Access to target systems and services (e.g., AD, application APIs).
  • Predefined access rules and mappings.
  • Secure execution environment for script operations.

NOTES

  • Ensure all scripts follow Keyera’s security, audit, and change control policies.
  • Include retry logic and alerting for failed or partial executions.
  • This enhancement is a foundational step toward full automation of access provisioning workflows.
item.summary: FR-13 Orchestration Server will run scripts that configure access to approved security groups

comments.comment: Jordan Richter has mostly completed these tasks

Jordan Richter Please document all work to date or attach other tickets or Confluence pages, address any requirements in the ticket that haven’t been completed, and add any necessary information or tasks to facilitate cleanup of code to prepare for Prod deployment.

for clarity: ~95% of code used on both cgymsapp191 (FS prod PowerShell server) and cgymsapt188 (FreshLab (FL) sandbox PowerShell server) comes from Gopinath Duraiswamy’s initial PoC from 2024.

with that out of the way, the current functionalities for scripting are as follows:

  • Add to AD Group (Simple.Add to AD Group.ps1) - taking in passed username and AD group, it will attempt to add the user to the specified group. Errors accounted for include:
    • invalid user/group (hard with prior validation, but it’s possible nonetheless)
    • existing admission to group
    • other AD-related errors (e.g. service account doesn’t have permissions to modify the given security group)
    • other unexpected errors
  • Remove from AD Group (Simple.Remove from AD Group.ps1) - taking in passed username and AD group, it will attempt to remove the user from the specified group. Errors accounted for include:
    • invalid user/group (hard with prior validation, but it’s possible nonetheless)
    • lack of existing admission to group
    • other AD-related errors (e.g. service account doesn’t have permissions to modify the given security group)
    • other unexpected errors
  • Add to Azure AD Group (Simple.Add to Azure AD Group.ps1) - taking in passed username and AD group, it will attempt to add the user to the specified group. Errors accounted for include:
    • existing admission to group
    • other unexpected errors

the main functionality we’ve added is the SCIMapping.ps1 file and Search-SCI function contained within the Common.Magic Spells.psm1 file.

  1. SCIMapping provides a layer of security (requested by Mike Hughesman) that obfuscates the full security group until it reaches the server. This file creates a reference look-up key-value pair where the partial group name sent from FS is then translated to the full group for the file
  2. the Search-SCI function uses the above mapping file to complete the look-up to the proper security group

NOTE: the Convert-HtmlTableToPowerShellObject function is currently commented out as while the functionality works if the file is run on the server, it’s not working through FS. as no tickets currently have fields, we have not found the need to enable this at this time

A bit more info about the added code.

SCIMapping.ps1

This contains all currently created Data Foundation (DF) security groups and connects them to truncated versions of themselves that match what are sent over from the workflow automator from FS. For example, "MEA_ALL_APPS_VIEWER_IN" = "SG_ALL_IT_DF_MEA_ALL_APPS_VIEWER_IN", where "MEA_ALL_APPS_VIEWER_IN" comes from the custom object in FS, and "SG_ALL_IT_DF_MEA_ALL_APPS_VIEWER_IN" is the full security group (SG) name that the Add-ADGroupMember PowerShell function needs to do its job.

This needs to be updated every time a group is created.

Search-SCI Function

Something I made, hehe. Takes in one parameter ($SCIRequestGroup) which is the aforementioned shortened SG name. Then it imports the entire SCIMapping file and matches the $SCIRequestGroup to $groupname, which it returns. Nothing too fancy, but then it’s programatic. This code is located in the Common.Magic Spells.psm1 file

item.title: [DF-445] FR-11 FreshService will call Orchestration Server to automate tasks (such as adding users to AD groups)
item.description:
DESCRIPTION

Enhance FreshService integration by enabling it to call the Orchestration Server to automate downstream tasks—such as adding users to Active Directory (AD) groups—based on Service Catalogue Item (SCI) workflows. This automation will streamline fulfillment of product requests and reduce manual effort.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA

  • FreshService workflows are configured to trigger calls to the Orchestration Server for applicable SCIs.
  • The API call includes all required parameters (e.g., user ID, group ID, request context).
  • The Orchestration Server accepts the request and returns a success or failure response.
  • Success responses are logged and optionally included in the FreshService ticket.
  • Failure responses are logged and surfaced to administrators with actionable error messages.
  • The system ensures idempotency to prevent duplicate provisioning actions.
  • Process is well documented in Confluence.

OUT OF SCOPE

  • Manual execution of orchestration tasks.
  • Orchestration logic unrelated to SCI-based requests.

DEPENDENCIES

  • Orchestration Server endpoint and credentials.
  • Defined API contract between FreshService and the Orchestration Server.
  • SCI workflows configured to support automation triggers.

NOTES

  • Ensure secure transmission of sensitive data (e.g., via HTTPS and token-based auth). https://keyera.atlassian.net/browse/DF-453
  • Consider retry logic and alerting for failed orchestration attempts.
  • This enhancement supports scalable, automated access provisioning and aligns with ITSM best practices.
item.summary: FR-11 FreshService will call Orchestration Server to automate tasks (such as adding users to AD groups)

comments.comment:
The SR: Invoke Automation for Service Requests ticket automator has been enabled with the following payload being sent to the PowerShell server

pwsh -File "D:\Freshservice\Orchestration\Powershell\Scripts\Orchestration.Facade.ps1" {{service_desk_url ticket.id ticket.actual_requester.email ticket.service_request_item_names ticket.visible_service_item_fields R2.group_nameR3.script_file_name -Verbose -Restart}}

The parameters in detail being passed are:

  1. {{service_desk_url}} - the URL of the ticket (e.g. https://keyfreshlab.freshservice.com/a/tickets/432)
  2. {{ticket.id}} - the ticket number (e.g. 432)
  3. {{ticket.actual_requester.email}} - the email of the user requested for (needed for the SAML translation in the script, e.g. jordan_richter@keyera.com)
  4. {{ticket.service_request_item_names}} - the name of the SCI (e.g. Fundamentals | Business Users | Access Package - Add)
  5. {{ticket.visible_service_item_fields}} - any entered fields in an SCI submitted through this process (no e.g. right now since none of the SCIs at the time of writing (July 14th, 2025) have any fields needing to be processed)
  6. {{R2.group_name}} - the workflow reader (in this case, the one reading the definition of the automation specifics from the SR Automation - Adding or Removing Users to AD Groups custom object) grabbing the group that the SCI is set up to modify access to (e.g. FUN_ALL_APPS_DEVELOPER_IN)
    1. this is translated to the full group name on server side using the SCIMapping.ps1 file
  7. {{R3.script_file_name}} - with using the friendly name the workflow gets from R2 (just above), it compares it against the Automation Script Pairing custom object and passes the ps file name (e.g. Simple.Add to AD Group.ps1)

Error handling is accounted for right after

item.title: [DF-443] FR-9 FreshService will have a group of defined workflows and automations for processing every SCI
item.description:
DESCRIPTION

Enhance FreshService by establishing a standardized (as best we can) set of workflows and automations to process every Service Catalogue Item (SCI) consistently. These workflows will streamline the handling of FreshService requests and ensure that each SCI follows a predictable, auditable process from submission to fulfillment.

This enhancement supports automation, reduces manual intervention, and improves service delivery consistency.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA

  • A defined workflow exists for each SCI in FreshService.
  • Workflows include steps such as approval routing, group assignment, and ticket resolution.
  • Automations are configured to trigger based on SCI-specific criteria (e.g., product type, requester role).
  • Notifications are sent to relevant stakeholders at key stages (e.g., request received, approved, fulfilled).
  • Each workflow logs actions for audit purposes.
  • Errors or exceptions in workflow execution are logged and surfaced to administrators.

OUT OF SCOPE

  • Manual ticket handling outside of defined workflows.
  • Integration with external systems beyond FreshService (unless explicitly required by the SCI).

DEPENDENCIES

  • Access to FreshService admin console for workflow configuration.
  • Complete and accurate SCI definitions.
  • Defined business rules for each SCI’s fulfillment process.

NOTES

  • Consider using FreshService’s workflow automator and scenario automations for implementation.
  • Align workflows with existing ITSM practices and compliance requirements.
  • This enhancement lays the groundwork for scalable, automated access provisioning.
item.summary: FR-9 FreshService will have a group of defined workflows and automations for processing every SCI

comments.comment: Jordan Richter has already done a lot of this so likely we just need to define the process in Confluence.

Process has been largely taken from Gopi’s original workflow with minor additions

general steps are as follows:

  1. ticket has been moved out of pending approval (has been approved)
  2. the overall “kill switch” on automation is checked (should be false)
    1. there’s a setting in the Generic Pairing Look Up custom object that allows us to shut off all automation in case there’s an issue
  3. the specific SCI’s entry on the SR Automation _ Adding or Removing Users to AD Groups custom object is checked to verify automation is currently enabled (should be yes)
    1. similar to the previous step, this allows for a more granular approach for specific SCIs so that we don’t have to nuke an SCI if it’s misbehaving, we can just disable its automation if needed
  4. the available PowerShell scripts are defined
  5. it’s assigned to the Data Storefront Admins group
  6. the script is called with the defined payload
    • pwsh -File "D:\Freshservice\Orchestration\Powershell\Scripts\Orchestration.Facade.ps1" {{service_desk_url ticket.id ticket.actual_requester.email "ticket.service_request_item_names" "R3.script_file_name" "R2.group_name" -Verbose -Restart}}
  7. the result is processed
    1. if errors, it emails the admins
    2. if no errors, continue
  8. evaluate the resulting text
  9. check if this kind of request type should be closed automatically
    1. the functionality just exists in case there’s some level of manual evaluation required or just even for debugging
    2. if yes, continue
  10. does it need to wait for 15 minutes before resolving in case people get overzealous with checking their access right away? (usually for AD propagation allowances)
    1. if no, resolve right away
    2. if yes, continue
  11. does it actually need to wait 30 minutes (again, just for allowances)
    1. if no, start a 15 minute timer, then resolve
    2. if yes, start a 30 minute timer, then resolve
    3. this could be modified/chained as need be to account for different allowances

item.title: [DF-442] FR-8 FreshService will have a service catalogue item (SCI) for every item in the DUC+

item.title: [DF-440] FR-6 Data Storefront will GET FreshService service catalog items flat file and store it in a folder accessible to Data Menu every day at 5:30 am
item.description:
Description

Automate the retrieval of FreshService service catalog items by configuring the Data Storefront to perform a daily GET request at 5:30 AM from FreshService. The response, a flat file containing the catalog data, will be stored in a designated folder accessible to the Data Menu for processing and display.

Acceptance Criteria

  • A scheduled job runs daily at 5:30 AM to perform a GET request to the FreshService API.
  • The API call retrieves the full list of service catalog items in flat file format (JSON).
  • The file is saved to a predefined folder accessible by the Data Menu.
  • The job logs success/failure status and any relevant metadata (e.g., timestamp, file size).
  • Errors in the API call or file write process are logged and trigger alerts.
  • There is no predefined requirement for how to do the integration.

Out of Scope

  • Parsing or transforming the catalog data for display.
  • Manual triggering of the job.

Dependencies

  • FreshService API credentials and endpoint access.
  • File storage location with read access for the Data Menu.
  • Scheduling infrastructure (e.g., cron job, task scheduler, or cloud function).
  • https://keyera.atlassian.net/browse/DF-471

Notes

  • Ensure the job handles API rate limits and retries gracefully.
  • Consider versioning or timestamping the saved files for traceability.
  • This feature supports the Data Menu’s ability to present daily updates of the service catalog.
item.summary: FR-6 Data Storefront will GET FreshService service catalog items flat file and store it in a folder accessible to Data Menu every day at 5:30 am

comments.comment: Jordan Richter Can you please include the API call you were using from Postman to FreshService in this ticket?
Could be assigned to Jordan if he has time.

so the basic GET call looks like https://keyfreshlab.freshservice.com/api/v2/service_catalog/items (for production, it would likely be https://keyera.freshservice.com/api/v2/service_catalog/items). but, as we’re likely going to be specifically looking at the workspace that we contain the data storefront items in, at least for the time being, you can include the parameter of workspace_id to specify that.

that’ll end up looking like https://choosecorrectsubdomain.freshservice.com/api/v2/service_catalog/items?workspace_id=4

Currently, the implementation uses a cron job scheduled to run at a set interval to send a GET request for catalog items. The retrieved data is then written to a JSON file, which is consumed by the components. This approach is intended to minimize the number of requests and stay within rate limits.

For development purposes, I’ve run the job manually once to fetch the initial data, since no new data products are being added at the moment. In production, this will be properly orchestrated to run on a recurring schedule as planned.
During deployment we can decide how we want to run the cron job.

item.title: [DF-439] FR-5 Data Storefront will show a list of the customer’s tickets/PARs (receipt list)
item.description:
DESCRIPTION

Enhance the Data Menu functionality to display a list of the customer’s Product Access Requests (PARs), effectively serving as a receipt list. This view will allow users to track their submitted requests and view relevant details such as status, submission date, and associated product.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA

  • A new section or tab is available in the Data Storefront labeled “My Requests” or similar.
  • The list displays all tickets sourced from FreshService for the Data Foundations catalog submitted by the current user.
  • Each entry includes key details: product name, request date, status, and ticket ID (if applicable).
  • The list is sorted by most recent request by default.
  • Clicking or expanding an entry optionally expands or links to more detailed request information.
  • If no requests exist, a friendly empty state message is shown.
  • Errors in loading the list are logged and surfaced to the user with a clear message.

OUT OF SCOPE

  • Editing or canceling existing tickets from the receipt list.
  • Displaying tickets submitted by other users or on behalf of other users

DEPENDENCIES

  • Backend API endpoint to retrieve tickets for the current user.
  • Authentication context to identify the current user.
  • UI component library support for list rendering and empty states.

NOTES

  • Ensure the list is responsive and accessible.
  • Consider pagination or lazy loading for users with many requests.
  • This feature improves transparency and reduces support inquiries by allowing users to self-verify their access requests.
item.summary: FR-5 Data Storefront will show a list of the customer’s tickets/PARs (receipt list)
