I successfully implemented a comprehensive Request Receipts feature that integrates with the Freshservice API to display user service requests with enhanced service catalog information. I built three main components working together: a backend API endpoint, frontend data processing, and intelligent service matching. On the backend, I created a GET route /api/service-catalog/requests that fetches tickets from Freshservice using the existing authentication credentials and HTTPS agent configuration, querying tickets for a specific user email with workspace filtering. I designed the frontend RequestReceipts component to load data from two sources simultaneously - fetching real-time ticket data from my backend API and loading the local services.json file containing the complete service catalog. The core challenge I faced was matching ticket data with service descriptions since Freshservice tickets don't contain direct service IDs. I solved this by parsing the ticket subject line, which follows the format "Request for [user] : [service_name]", extracting the service name and matching it against the service catalog by name. This approach allows me to enrich each ticket with detailed service information including descriptions, display IDs, and metadata. I implemented proper status mapping for Freshservice status codes (2=Open, 3=Pending, 4=Resolved, 5=Closed, 6=Pending Approval) with corresponding color coding for visual distinction. I designed the UI with a modern two-panel layout featuring filtering capabilities, where I parse service names and display them in a hierarchical format (Domain | Service Type) while filtering out generic role terms like "Business Users" and "Everyone" for cleaner presentation. I ensured the component handles loading states, error scenarios, and provides real-time data synchronization between the ticket system and service catalog, resulting in a comprehensive receipt management system that gives users full visibility into their service requests with rich contextual information.

const handleRequest = async (item: ServiceItem): Promise<void> => {

Integrated a post request in ServiceCard.tsx to send a structured payload to the backend. The payload includes the selected service's ID, the user's email, and the selected quantity. This allows the backend to accurately process, and track service selections initiated from the frontend. In simple terms, this enables the request access button to do stuff.

router.post('/create', async (req, res) => {
    try {
        // Get the request data sent from frontend
        const { email, quantity, displayId } = req.body;
        console.log(`Creating service for ${email} with quantity ${quantity} for service ${displayId}`);
        
        // Get Freshservice connection details from environment variables
        const apiKey = process.env.FRESHSERVICE_API_KEY;   // Your API key
        const baseUrl = process.env.FRESHSERVICE_BASE_URL; // Freshservice URL
        
        // Create authentication credentials for Freshservice
        // Freshservice uses Basic Auth with format: "apikey:X" encoded in base64
        const credentials = Buffer.from(`${apiKey}:X`).toString('base64');
        
        // Create HTTPS agent to handle SSL connections
        // rejectUnauthorized: false skips SSL certificate validation (for corporate networks)
        const httpsAgent = new (require('https').Agent)({
            rejectUnauthorized: false
        });
        
        // Make API call to Freshservice using the specific service display_id in URL
        const freshserviceResponse = await axios.post(`${baseUrl}/service_catalog/items/${displayId}/place_request`, {
            // Request details to send to Freshservice
            email: email,                              // Who is requesting the service
            quantity: quantity                         // How many instances requested
        }, {
            // Request configuration
            headers: {
                'Authorization': `Basic ${credentials}`,  // Authentication header
                'Content-Type': 'application/json'        // Tell server we're sending JSON
            },
            httpsAgent  // Use our custom HTTPS handler
        });
        
        // Send success response back to frontend
        res.status(200).json({
            message: 'Service request created successfully',
            requestId: freshserviceResponse.data.service_request.id,  // Return the service request ID
            subject: freshserviceResponse.data.service_request.subject // Return the request subject
        });
        
    } catch (error: any) {
        // If anything goes wrong, log the error and send error response
        console.error('Error creating ticket:', error.message);
        res.status(500).json({ error: 'Failed to create service request' });
    }
});

Implemented a POST request that sends a structured payload from the frontend and returns the response body to the frontend. The returned data will be used to dynamically update the UI. For now, the implementation remains minimal while we await further guidance on which response fields will be utilized.

1. User clicks Request button on service card
  2. handleRequest function triggers with item data
  3. Frontend extracts item.display_id from the service
  4. Frontend creates JSON payload with displayId, email, quantity
  5. Frontend sends POST request to localhost:3001/api/service-catalog/create
  6. Request travels over network to backend server
  7. Express server receives request on port 3001
  8. Express matches /api/service-catalog/create route
  9. Backend extracts email, quantity, displayId from req.body
  10. Backend loads environment variables for API credentials
  11. Backend creates Basic Auth credentials string
  12. Backend sets up HTTPS agent for SSL handling
  13. Backend makes axios POST to Freshservice API with displayId in URL
  14. Request sent to baseUrl/service_catalog/items/357/place_request
  15. Freshservice receives and processes the service request
  16. Freshservice creates service request in their system
  17. Freshservice returns JSON response with service_request object
  18. Backend receives freshserviceResponse.data from Freshservice
  19. Backend extracts service_request.id and service_request.subject
  20. Backend creates response object with message, requestId, subject
  21. Backend sends res.status(200).json() back to frontend
  22. HTTP response travels back over network to frontend
  23. Frontend receives response from fetch call
  24. Frontend calls await response.json() to parse JSON
  25. Frontend gets data object with message, requestId, subject
  26. Frontend checks if response.ok is true
  27. Frontend accesses data.requestId for the service request ID
  28. Frontend shows alert with success message and request ID
  29. User sees confirmation that request was submitted successfully

Preventing duplicates idea:

Since you will be requesting the “my requests” list from Freshservice at least one time when accessing the website, you could use the complete list of IDs to grey out or change buttons for items that have already been requested to green and say “Already Requested”. You’d only do this for requests in the completed or pending status and where approval is either complete or not needed.

I have successfully implemented a feature that prevents user from requesting items they have already requested.

// Store existing user requests to check for duplicates
const [existingRequests, setExistingRequests] = useState<any[]>([]);

useEffect(() => {
  const loadData = async () => {
    try {
      // Fetch service data from static JSON
      const servicesResponse = await fetch('/services.json');
      const servicesData = await servicesResponse.json();
      setServices(servicesData.service_items || servicesData);
      
      // Fetch existing user requests
      const requestsResponse = await fetch('http://localhost:3001/api/service-catalog/requests');
      const requestsData = await requestsResponse.json();
      if (requestsData.success) {
        setExistingRequests(requestsData.tickets || []);
      }
    } catch (error) {
      console.error('Error loading data:', error);
    } finally {
      setLoading(false);
    }
  };
  
  loadData();
}, []);
 
// Helper function to convert status numbers to text
const getStatusText = (status: number): string => {
  switch (status) {
    case 2: return 'Open';
    case 3: return 'Pending';
    case 4: return 'Resolved';
    case 5: return 'Closed';
    case 6: return 'Pending Approval';
    default: return 'Unknown';
  }
};

// Check if this service has already been requested
const isAlreadyRequested = existingRequests.some(request => {
  const serviceNameMatch = request.subject?.match(/Request for .+ : (.+)$/);
  const requestedServiceName = serviceNameMatch ? serviceNameMatch[1].trim() : null;
  return requestedServiceName === item.name;
});

// Request button with duplicate prevention
<button 
  onClick={async () => {
    if (isAlreadyRequested) return;
    // ... request logic
  }}
  disabled={isAlreadyRequested}
  style={{
    backgroundColor: isAlreadyRequested ? '#28a745' : '#004B87',
    // ... other styles
  }}
>
  {isAlreadyRequested ? (
    <>
      <svg>/* checkmark icon */</svg>
      Already Requested
    </>
  ) : (
    <>
      <svg>/* plus icon */</svg>
      Request Access
    </>
  )}
</button>

comments.comment: Eric Mah along with Lee Palisoc have already designed the feature. We need to address some of the other pieces like error handling, etc if not handled already.

import axios from 'axios';
import fs from 'fs';
import path from 'path';
import dotenv from 'dotenv';

dotenv.config();

const fetchAndSaveServices = async () => {
  try {
    const apiKey = process.env.FRESHSERVICE_API_KEY;
    const baseUrl = process.env.FRESHSERVICE_BASE_URL;
    const workspaceId = process.env.WORKSPACE_ID;

    if (!apiKey || !baseUrl) {
      throw new Error('Missing API configuration');
    }

    const credentials = Buffer.from(`${apiKey}:X`).toString('base64');
    const headers = {
      'Authorization': `Basic ${credentials}`
    };
    const httpsAgent = new (require('https').Agent)({
      rejectUnauthorized: false
    });
    
    // Fetch all service items
    const response = await axios.get(`${baseUrl}/service_catalog/items`, {
      params: { workspace_id: workspaceId },
      headers,
      httpsAgent
    });

    const serviceItems = response.data.service_items || [];
    console.log(`Fetching details for ${serviceItems.length} services...`);

    // Fetch individual service details and append desc_un_html
    const enhancedServices = await Promise.all(
      serviceItems.map(async (service: any) => {
        try {
          const detailResponse = await axios.get(`${baseUrl}/service_catalog/items/${service.display_id}`, {
            headers,
            httpsAgent
          });
          
          return {
            ...service,
            desc_un_html: detailResponse.data.service_item.desc_un_html || null
          };
        } catch (error: any) {
          console.warn(`Failed to fetch details for service ${service.display_id}:`, error.message);
          return {
            ...service,
            desc_un_html: null
          };
        }
      })
    );

    // Path to frontend public directory
    const frontendPath = path.join(__dirname, '../../frontend/public/services.json');
    
    // Write enhanced data to JSON file
    const enhancedData = {
      ...response.data,
      service_items: enhancedServices
    };
    
    fs.writeFileSync(frontendPath, JSON.stringify(enhancedData, null, 2));
    
    console.log(`Services data updated at ${new Date().toISOString()}`);
    console.log(`Saved ${enhancedServices.length} services with descriptions`);
    
  } catch (error: any) {
    console.error('Error fetching services:', error.message);
  }
};

// Run immediately if called directly
if (require.main === module) {
  fetchAndSaveServices();
}

export { fetchAndSaveServices };

Services are fetched from Freshservice and parsed into a json for easy extraction by components.
Maybe we can evaluate whether the metadata we provide for the data products in sufficient.

item.title: [DF-422] Document General Architectural Principles & Best Practices

item.title: [DF-404] x-Ingest Data from Source System
item.description:
We have already completed ingestion of some TIPS data that is now available as bronze and silver tables. However, to complete this data product, we need to extend and modify the tables we are ingesting.

  • Table: QRMTIPS.QCTRL_PLANT_HDR – This table has plant names associated to plant codes.

Ingestion covers connecting to source systems, creating bronze tables and extracting data into those tables, cleaning the data, and loading it into silver tables. Note: It does not include the application of business logic or the creation of gold tables.

Please provide a description of the source systems and the tables that will be ingested, along with any technical requirements. If the Data Product requires more than one source system or requires multiple steps to connect and stage the data, we may need to create more than one story. Use the questions below to guide your work.

  • What source systems are we ingesting from?
  • What method are we using to connect to those systems?
  • Are the data sources relatively easy to access or do they require extra development to connect (e.g., is it an internal system with an accessible database, does it have an object model that makes it difficult to query, do we need to pull the data from an API and do we have access)?
  • What is the necessary refresh cadence?
  • What is the desired ingest granularity?
  • What is the structure of the source system data?
  • Are there data quality considerations that need to be overcome?
  • What are the characteristics of the source data that we need to be aware of (e.g., refresh cadence, quality, granularity)?
  • How clean is the source data and does it conform to Keyera standards (e.g., quality, units of measure)?
item.summary: x-Ingest Data from Source System

item.title: [DF-400] Define Data Product Requirements
item.description:
Use the questions below to guide business requirements. In combination with our Technical Standards, these form the functional and non-functional requirements.

  • Define
    • What data do we think we need to solve the business problem?
    • What other factors besides data might need to be addressed to solve the problem?
  • Ingest
    • What sources have the data that we think is needed?
    • What are the characteristics of the source data that we need to be aware of (e.g., refresh cadence, quality, granularity)?
    • Are the data sources relatively easy to access or do they require extra development to connect (e.g., is it an internal system with an accessible database, does it have an object model that makes it difficult to query, do we need to pull the data from an API and do we have access)?
  • Transform
    • What is the shape of the source data and what shape is needed in the final product?
    • How clean is the source data and does it conform to Keyera standards (e.g., quality, units of measure)?
    • Does the data need to be normalized or joined with other data sets to be useful?
  • Process
    • Is the source data already well understood, or does it require exploration and manipulation by a senior data analyst?
    • Is a single set of final “gold” tables sufficient, or is there value in providing access to some intermediate date sets?
    • How will the data be used (e.g., internal analysis, machine learning, presentation to end users)?
  • Consume
    • Who is the audience for the data?
    • Does the data include sensitive or confidential information?
    • How does the business intend to consume the data (e.g., Excel, Power BI, Databricks Dashboard, or will it feed into another system)?
item.summary: Define Data Product Requirements

item.title: [DF-384] Gold 4: Creating the G&P ACCTG - References table(s)
item.description:
As the TIPS data owner, I need to present TIPS codes with their names/descriptions to users as a Databricks table (or a set of tables) so that users can understand TIPS data and reports.

Technical details:

Various G&P data products use codes to identify volume types, meter types and so on. TIPS contains a separate table per code type, each table including the code itself, its description and - in most cases - the last updated time stamp. This data can be presented to users as a set of tables of a similar structure (Code, Code Description, Last Update), or as one table, with an additional column for a a code type (Code Type, Code, Code Description, Last Update). The main use of this data is to help users work with TIPS data.

Potentially, this data can be used by other TIPS data products, for resolving codes to their names/descriptions.

The reference tables are listed in this item: ​https://keyera.atlassian.net/browse/DF-44

Metadata file with data examples: Production_Accounting_Product_Metadata.xlsx

Queries (per code type): Gold additional tables - TIPS.docx

item.title: [DF-379] Gold 7: TIPS to Q2 Meter Mapping Table
item.description:
As a Business Development (BD) Rep, I need to map TIPS meters to Q2 daily volume tags so that I can reconcile meter data from these two applications.

Business context (optional reading):

TIPS and Q2 meters are the same physical meters, but known under different names in those applications and associated with different data elements: TIPS provides customer allocation on meters, and Q2 provides volume and composition on the same meters. Upon reconciling the meter data, BDs can estimate allocated month-to-date volumes (with composition) to customer, before these volumes are posted in TIPS. This data will be presented in Customer Volume Projection table.

Technical context (optional reading):

For the purpose of this initiative, we only need to map the unique ID of a TIPS meter to the unique ID of the same meter in Q2. However for usability, the mapping needs to be enhanced with meter properties from each app, such as plant, product, parent device, description etc. To avoid the “garbage-in” situation, TIPS meter properties can be retrieved from the Meter Hierarchy table (keyera_enterprise_prod.gold_tips.meter_hierarchy) in Databricks. Q2 meter properties can be retrieved from MMS tables (public.measurement_tag and public.measurement_tag_suffix).

Details:

  1. Create a gold TIPS-Q2 meter mapping table in Databricks, as per product definition: https://keyera.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/DF/pages/87687169/TIPS-Q2+Meter+Mapping. Also, there is a mock-up destination table with TIPS-Q2 data mapping here : keyera_temporary.sandbox.tips_q2_mapping_manual. Please note that the table is not exact, just a rough draft. Use the product definition in Confluence as a final reference.
  2. Populate the table as follows:
  3. Bring the key columns from silver_sharepoint_site_data_foundations.tips_q2_meter_mapping (all columns):https://keyera.atlassian.net/browse/DF-789
  • TIPS Meter #
  • Q2 Tag ID
  • Updated By
  • Updated On
  1. Add TIPS meter properties to the TIPS-Q2 meter mapping table:
    For each TIPS meter #, find a records of that meter # in keyera_enterprise_prod.gold_tips.meter_hierarchy for the most recent combination of Production Period (PROD_DT) and Accounting Period (ACCT_DT) and populate the following properties:
  • Production Period
  • Accounting Period
  • TIPS Plant Code
  • TIPS Plant Name
  • TIPS Parent       
  • TIPS Meter #
  • TIPS Product
  • TIPS Plant Meter
  • TIPS Meter Description
  • TIPS Meter UOM

If TIPS meter # can’t be found in the meter hierarchy table, populate all the fields with “Not found in TIPS meter hierarchy”.

  1. Add Q2 tag properties to the TIPS-Q2 meter mapping table:
    For each Q2 Tag ID, retrieve the following properties from public.measurement_tag and public.measurement_tag_suffix tables (exact mapping to be specified after https://keyera.atlassian.net/browse/DF-688 ):
  • Q2 Product
  • Q2 Parent Device ID
  • Q2 Device Description
  • Q2 UOM

If a tag can’t be found in any of the two tables, populate the fields with “Not found in Q2 tags”.

Acceptance Criteria

  • The TIPS-Q2 meter mapping table exists in Databricks with accurate data.
  • The TIPS-Q2 meter mapping table in Databricks can be updated on demand.

Definition of Done:

  • Code is Written and Reviewed via Pull Request
  • Code Passes Unit Tests
  • Solution is Documented (README, docstrings, etc.).
  • Terraform is Updated (to create resource dependencies like groups, Service Principals, catalogs, schemas, etc.)
  • Development Deployment is Validated
  • Story is Attached to a Release
  • Release is Deployed to Test
item.summary: Gold 7: TIPS to Q2 Meter Mapping Table

Business context: The purpose of this table is to calculate the historical proportion of the customer's volume at the TIPS meter and the NGL yields. The historical proportions are averaged over a 1-, 3- and 6-month period so that analysis can be adjusted.

The data in this table is calculated from data in ​https://keyera.atlassian.net/browse/DF-377.

item.title: [DF-376] Gold 1: Creating G&P ACCTG - Posted Volumes table
item.description:
As a TIPS data owner, I need to have TIPS posted volumes published as a table in Databricks, so that other business group and users can use it as an input into their processes and Databricks products.

Business context: This table tracks details related to the production, distribution, and consumption of various volume-based commodities, such as gas, liquid, or other products. It provides a view of working interest ownership by settlement meter, customer, and product for each historical posted period.

The following details needs to be included in the table:

# Column Name Description Value source
(as per the query below, unless specified differently)
1 Plant Name A plant name Not in the query
QRMTIPS.QCTRL_PLANT_HDR.PLANT_NM
Needs to be resolved from the plant code through the Plant Header table (most recent record for the plant code from QRMTIPS.QCTRL_PLANT_HDR).
Depends on https://keyera.atlassian.net/browse/DF-421
2 Plant Code A unique TIPS ID of the plant for which the volume was posted qrmtips.qpost_alloc_vol.plant_no
3 Accounting Period The accounting period for which the volume was posted qrmtips.qpost_alloc_vol.acct_dt
4 Production Period The production period when the volume was posted qrmtips.qpost_alloc_vol.prod_d
5 Unit of Time Code The time interval for which the volume was posted qrmtips.qpost_alloc_vol.unit_tm_cd
6 TIPS Meter Number A unique ID of a meter in TIPS where the posted volume was measured qrmtips.qpost_alloc_vol.mtr_no
7 TIPS Meter Name A TIPS name of the meter where the posted volume was measured qrmtips.qpost_paystation.mtr_nm
8 TIPS Meter Suffix A suffix identifying a customer’s share of the product measured on the meter qrmtips.qpost_alloc_vol.mtr_sfx
9 Contract Number A customer’s contract to flow volumes through the TIPS meter (from eOne) qrmtips.qpost_paystation.ctr_no
10 BA ID The BA ID of the customer owning the product on the meter qrmtips.qpost_paystation.ctr_party_ba_no
11 BA Name The name of the customer owning the product on the meter qrmtips.qctrl_ba_entity.ctr_party_ba_nm1
12 Accounting Meter Type Code The type of the meter where the volume were measured qrmtips.qpost_paystation.acct_mtr_type_cd, 
include only records where ACCT_MTR_TYPE_CD = 'SL' (settlement)
13 Record Status Code The record status code qrmtips.qpost_alloc_vol.rec_status_cd
15 Record Status Description The record status description Not in the query
QRMTIPS.QCODE_REC.REC_STATUS_DESCR
Depends on https://keyera.atlassian.net/browse/DF-276
resolved based on records status code
16 Product Code The product code associated with the volume qrmtips.qpost_alloc_vol.prod_cd
17 Product Name The product name not in the query
QRMTIPS.QCODE_PRODUCT.prod_descr
resolved based on product code
18 Disposition Code The disposition code associated with the volume qrmtips.qpost_alloc_vol.disp_cd
19 Disposition Description The disposition description associated with the volume Not in the query
QRMTIPS.QCODE_DISPOSITION DISP_DESCR
resolved based on disposition code
Depends on https://keyera.atlassian.net/browse/DF-276
20 Volume Type Code The volume type code associated with the volume qrmtips.qpost_alloc_vol.vol_type_cd
21 Volume Type Description The volume type description associated with the volume Not in the query
VOL_TYPE_DESCRQRMTIPS.QCODE_VOL_TYPE
resolved based on volume type code
22 Actual Gas Volume The actual gas volume qrmtips.qpost_alloc_vol.gas_vol
23 Actual Gas Volume UOM The actual gas volume UOM Not in the query
If there is a value in Actual Gas Volume, populate with e3m3.
24 Heat Value The heat content or energy value of the gas qrmtips.qpost_alloc_vol.heat_value
25 Heat Value UOM   Not in the query
If there is a value in Heat Value, populate with GJ.
26 Actual Liquid Volume The actual liquid volume qrmtips.qpost_alloc_vol.liq_vol
27 Actual Liquid Volume UOM The actual liquid volume UOM Not in the query
If there is a value in Actual Liquid Volume, populate with m3.
28 Theoretical Gas Volume The theoretical gas volume (based on components coming to the facility). qrmtips.qpost_alloc_vol.theo_gas_vol
29 Theoretical Gas Volume UOM The theoretical gas volume UOM Not in the query
If there is a value in Theoretical Gas Volume, populate with e3m3.
30 Theoretical Heat Value The theoretical heat content or energy value of the gas (based on components coming to the facility) qrmtips.qpost_alloc_vol.theo_heat_value
31 Theoretical Heat Value UOM   Not in the query
If there is a value in Theoretical Heat Value, populate with GJ.
32 Theoretical Liquid Volume The theoretical liquid volume (expressed in m3) - based on components coming to the facility qrmtips.qpost_alloc_vol.theo_liq_vol
33 Theoretical Liquid Volume UOM   Not in the query
If there is a value in Theoretical Liquid Volume, populate with m3.
34 Sulphur Sulphur content qrmtips.qpost_alloc_vol.other_qty
(this column can capture any other relevant product component, and in our case it refers to sulphur (expressed in tonnes)
35 Sulphur UOM   Not in the query
If there is a value in Sulphur, populate with tonnes.
36 Allocation Group Number The Allocation Group Number (= set of related volume records). qrmtips.qpost_alloc_vol.alloc_grp_no
37 Allocation Sequence The Allocation Sequence, or order of the volume record within the allocation group. qrmtips.qpost_alloc_vol.alloc_seq
38 Run Identifier A unique Run Identifier for the processing batch that the volume record is associated with qrmtips.qpost_alloc_vol.run_id
39 Physical/Contract Allocation Code Identifies whether the allocation is physical or contractually: P = Physical Allocation (only physical, no ownership), C = Contract Allocation (applies ownership to physical allocation) qrmtips.qpost_paystation.phys_ctr_cd
40 Parent Meter Number Links the volume record to a Parent Meter Number qrmtips.qpost_paystation.parent_mtr_no

Query:
This query produces most of the columns for this table: G&P Accounting - Posted Volume.docx
Data no longer needed from the query: Comp_cd, pct_contr.

Production_Accounting_Product_Metadata.xlsx > G&P Accounting - Posted Volumes tab

item.title: [DF-354] Assess naming of all workspaces, resources, groups, etc.
item.description:
• Do we really need everything to be prepended with “keyera?”
  • Can we rename the “keyera-<env>data-extraction” workspaces to something like “data-engineering<env>?” We use these workspaces for more than just ingest since the Gold tables are all defined here.
  • Can we rename the “keyera-<env>analytics-lakehouse-workspace” workspaces to something like “data-analysis<env>?”
  • etc.
item.summary: Assess naming of all workspaces, resources, groups, etc.

comments.comment:
I don’t recommend renaming the Databricks workspaces.

Including “Keyera” in the names follows common cloud standards, ensures globally unique identifiers, and helps future-proof resources for scenarios like mergers/acquisitions/joint ventures or data sharing. More importantly, Databricks workspaces cannot be renamed in place; renaming would require full recreation and migration of all assets, including some AWS resources.

Given the high cost and risk compared to the limited benefit, keeping the current naming convention is the most practical approach.

That said, we can do this. I just don’t think it aligns with the direction you want to be going.

Lee Pattison, can you chime in and let me know if you want to do this or reject the user story?
Lee Pattison , please change the status to either Rejected or Approved to Start, depending on what you want to do with it.

Zackary Oleitschuk Scott Drennan

Let’s not change the workspace names at this point. I don’t think the effort vs. reward is sufficient.

item.title: [DF-344] Production Deployment
item.description:
1. Infra (Joel) create private certificate for benny.keyera.com
  2. Application Deployment (Oliver) create AWS LB TLS listener using benny.keyera.com cert created in step 1.
  3. Infra (Joel) create CNAME record from benny.keyera.com to AWS LB TLS FQDN (output from step 2)
  4. Infra (Joel) create Azure AD enterprise application and SSO configuration
  5. App Deployment (Oliver) to run IaC script to deploy infrastructure for application (will deploy and configure all infrastructure on AWS)
  6. App Deployment (Oliver) to run Docker ECR deploy, to deploy application docker images to ECR
  7. TEST: team to validate proper function of application.

Here’s more detail if you need it:

Benny AI Chatbot - Initial Production Deployment Plan

Application Overview

Multi-region AI chatbot application with frontend in Canada and backend in Europe for data sovereignty compliance.

Architecture Components

Frontend (Canada - ca-central-1)

  • Nginx Load Balancer: Routes traffic and serves static content
  • React Frontend: User interface for chat interactions
  • Public ALB: Internet-facing load balancer

Backend (Europe - eu-central-1)

  • FastAPI Backend: Handles chat logic and AI processing
  • Internal ALB: Private load balancer for backend services
  • AWS Bedrock: AI/ML inference service
  • Secrets Manager: JWT tokens and configuration

Deployment Order

Phase 1: Infrastructure (Pre-deployed by SysAdmin)

  • VPCs and networking (both regions)
  • Security groups and VPC endpoints
  • Application Load Balancers
  • ECS clusters

Phase 2: Container Images

  1. Backend Image (eu-central-1)
    • Build and push to ECR: key-benny-backend:latest
  2. Frontend Image (ca-central-1)
    • Build and push to ECR: key-benny-frontend:latest
  3. Nginx Image (ca-central-1)
    • Build and push to ECR: key-benny-nginx:latest

Phase 3: Application Services

  1. Backend Service (eu-central-1)
    • ECS service with FastAPI backend
    • Connects to Bedrock for AI processing
    • Health check: /health endpoint
  2. Frontend Services (ca-central-1)
    • ECS service with Nginx + React frontend
    • Connects to backend in Europe
    • Health check: HTTP 200 on port 80

Phase 4: DNS & Traffic

  • Configure DNS to point to Canada ALB
  • Verify end-to-end connectivity

Key Configuration

Environment Variables

  • BACKEND_ALB_DNS: Internal backend endpoint
  • AZURE_AD_METADATA_URL: Authentication configuration
  • FRANKFURT_KNOWLEDGE_BASE_ID: Bedrock knowledge base

Secrets (Stored in Secrets Manager)

  • JWT_SECRET: Authentication token secret

Health Checks

  • Backend: http://backend-alb/health returns 200
  • Frontend: http://frontend-alb/ returns 200
  • End-to-end: Chat functionality works through UI

Rollback Plan

  • Scale ECS services to 0 desired count
  • Revert DNS if needed
  • Container images remain in ECR for quick restart

Estimated Deployment Time

  • Container builds: 15-20 minutes
  • Service deployment: 10-15 minutes
  • DNS propagation: 2-5 minutes
  • Total: ~30-40 minutes

item.title: [DF-337] Document Technical Standards for Power BI Integration
item.description:
Requirements

We must document technical standards for the integration of Power BI with Databricks. This should include:

  • Use of Service Principals in DB
  • Use of Service Accounts in PBI (or not)
  • Version control on Power BI reports (Dhruv)
  • Use of deployment pipelines in Power BI (or not) (Dhruv)
  • Access control Power BI workspaces and apps (Dhruv)
  • Local development access controls
  • Credential management and Personal Access Tokens
  • Best practices related to Native Queries vs. mCode vs. Dax (Dhruv)
  • Best practices related to Direct Query vs. Import (Dhruv)
  • Controls on other Fabric funtions (like Dataflows, data warehouse, etc.) - i.e. Where should work occur?
  • Best practices on use of paginated reports
  • Licencing for Power BI (pro users vs. premium workspaces) (Dhruv)
  • Guidelines on access non-databricks sources directly from Power BI
  • Use of Power BI vs. Databricks Dashboards
  • Connection of Excel to Semantic Models (Dhruv)
  • What services do we offer in Power BI?
  • Access Control & Networking Security with Power BI & Databricks (get reference from Dhruv)
  • Backup Strategy
  • Automation of necessary processes
  • Roles in workspaces in Power BI (Dhruv)

Note: This story does not include How-To documentation. Please capture needed or recommended how-to documentation elsewhere.

Success Criteria

A new Data Analyst or platform admin is able to consult our technical standards and setup a new workspace within Power BI, connect it to Databricks, and allow for local development of reports and successful publishing of the report to the Power BI service.

Note: All technical standard documentation must be reviewed and approved prior to being considered “done.”

item.title: [DF-336] Develop & Document Technical Standards
item.description:
We must document technical standards for the use of Databricks, AWS, integration with source systems, integration with Active Directory, and integration with downstream systems (e.g., Power BI). Each major section should be its own story.

Current TOC:

  • General Architecture Principles and Best Practices
    • Power BI is used for visualization.
    • Data modelling and transformation should be done as much as possible in Databricks.
    • We are BI agnostic. People can use Databricks Dashboards, Power BI, Visual KPI, Tableau, SAP BO, etc.
  • Visual KPI
    • Are we or aren't we?
  • Databricks Dashboards
    • Best practices
    • How-To Guides
    • Refresh cadence
  • Technical Standards for Integration with Power BI
    • Use of Service Principals in DB
    • Use of Service Accounts in PBI (or not)
    • Version control on Power BI reports
    • Use of deployment pipelines in Power BI (or not)
    • Access control Power BI workspaces and apps
    • Local development access controls
    • Credential management and Personal Access Tokens
    • Best practices related to Native Queries vs. mCode vs. Dax
    • Best practices related to Direct Query vs. Import
    • Controls on other Fabric funtions (like Dataflows, data warehouse, etc.) - i.e. Where should work occur?
    • Best practices on use of paginated reports
    • Licencing for Power BI (pro users vs. premium workspaces)
    • Guidelines on access non-databricks sources directly from Power BI
    • Use of Power BI vs. Databricks Dashboards
    • Connection of Excel to Semantic Models
    • What services do we offer in Power BI?
    • Access Control & Networking Security with Power BI & Databricks (get reference from Dhruv)
    • Backup Strategy
  • Cost Controls
    • Report refresh cadence (Databricks Dashboards or external)
    • AWS S3 Storage per team sandbox schema
  • Operational Reporting
    • Reports for external users
    • Real-time and near real-time reports
    • Row Level Security?
  • Ingestion Best Practices
    • Ingestion patterns from souce landscape and decision tree
      • Database direct query and snapshot
      • Change Data Capture (CDC)
      • Deltaflow Connectors
      • AWS Connectors (e.g., DCS)
      • Workado Orchestration?
      • External Storage Location
      • API ingestion
      • SharePoint ingestion
      • Network file ingestion
      • Blob ingestion and storage
    • We need a "Data Ingestion Cookbook"
    • Refresh cadence
    • Source database / system performance monitoring
    • Source database / system access controls
      • Use of Service Principals
      • Use of Service Accounts
      • Use of Developer Accounts for Data Analysis (as opposed to service accounts)
  • Medallion Architecture Best Practices
    • Bronze Data Best Practices
      • Import whole database and whole tables
      • Incremental updates
      • Append to last (preserve change history)
      • Import all fields as strings
    • Silver Data Best Practices
      • Enforce data types
      • NULL standard
      • Deduplication standard
    • Gold Data Best Practices
  • Databricks Platform Management
    • Workspaces
    • Users & Groups
    • Compute
    • Unity Catalog
    • Secret Stores
    • AWS Accounts
    • Backup Strategy
  • Security & Access
    • Business Access Packages
    • Data Access Packages
    • Use of Entra / Active Directory Groups
    • Use of APIM
    • FreshService Controls and Approvals
    • Single Service Account per App / Purpose
    • Role Scopes
  • Code & Deployment Management
    • SQL Best Practices
    • PySpark Best Practices
    • Code Repo Management
    • Deployment Permission Controls
    • Code Promotions
    • BitBucket Assessment

item.title: [DF-328] Automated testing for Sustainability dataset
item.description:
There are several dependencies (e.g. expected data types, foreign key relationships) within the Sustainability dataset sheets. As a result, any typos within the file can break the pipeline.

Proposed short-term solution: Add an automated test in the Bitbucket pipeline that validates the sustainability dataset before deployment so these errors are caught early. Bonus points if the business can run the validator on demand so they can validate their inputs.

A long-term solution could be a web app with validation built in the forms which would take more time and effort.

item.title: [DF-325] Add tests for utility functions
item.description:
Why:
The scd2 and Alteryx utility functions are critical components of the pipeline. Changes to these utilities can impact multiple downstream processes, potentially causing either visible pipeline failures or data integrity issues. To mitigate this risk, unit tests should be implemented to enable automated and manual regression testing.

Definition of Done:

  1. Unit tests are implemented for each utility function in:
  • src/utils/alteryx
  • src/utils/scd2
  1. The unit tests are configured to run automatically when a pull request is opened or updated.
  2. Devs can manually run the tests during local development to validate changes.
item.summary: Add tests for utility functions

item.title: [DF-321] Create separate Wapiti and Rimbey emissions dashboards
item.description:
Trying to merge Wapiti data with Rimbey into the current emissions dashboard is getting a bit complex since the different logic/sources between the two facilities is adding up. From the business’s perspective, it would be easier if there are different dashboards for each facility since each facility could have different quantifications as well (e.g. Production metric for Rimbey is Petrinex, while Wapiti uses ABGPI).

Tasks:

Emissions: Detailed Emissions (Rimbey) dashboard

  1. Rename “Emissions: Detailed Emissions (DAB)” → “Emissions: Detailed Emissions (DAB) - RIMBEY”
  2. Update dashboard so that only Rimbey data is displayed.

Emissions: Detailed Emissions (Wapiti) dashboard

  1. Create a clone of the emissions dashboard and name it “Emissions: Detailed Emissions (DAB) - WAPITI”
  2. For the Wapiti dashboard, make sure that only Wapiti data is displayed.
  3. Under the Compliance Summary metrics table, rename the “DISP (m3OE)” column → “ABGPI”
item.summary: Create separate Wapiti and Rimbey emissions dashboards

comments.comment: Hi Colton Reid - please feel free to add comments if there’s anything missing from the requirements.

06/04 Met with Colton Reid , Lee Pattison , Rekha, Scott Drennan

Decision 1: Keep one Detailed emissions dashboard for all facilities. Rename DISP (m3OE) to “Production Metric” and use tooltips to provide more context instead (e.g. “Wapiti: ABGPI (tCO2e), Rimbey: DISP (m3OE)”).

Decision 2: Create separate Operations dashboards for each facility for ease of use (future work).

item.title: [DF-305] Ingest TIPS Data per metadata product definition
item.description:
TIPS data pull query for Posted Volumes table:

SELECT v.plant_no, v.acct_dt, v.prod_dt, v.unit_tm_cd, v.mtr_no,

p.mtr_nm,

v.mtr_sfx,

p.ctr_no, p.ctr_party_ba_no,

e.ba_nm1,

p.acct_mtr_type_cd, v.rec_status_cd, v.prod_cd, v.disp_cd, v.comp_cd, v.vol_type_cd, v.gas_vol, v.heat_value, v.liq_vol, v.theo_gas_vol, v.theo_heat_value, v.theo_liq_vol,

v.other_qty, v.pct_contr, v.alloc_grp_no, v.alloc_seq,

v.run_id,

p.phys_ctr_cd, p.parent_mtr_no

from qrmtips.qpost_alloc_vol v

join qrmtips.qpost_paystation p on p.trnx_id = v.trnx_id and p.mtr_sfx = v.mtr_sfx

left join qrmtips.qctrl_ba_entity e on e.ba_no = p.ctr_party_ba_no

where v.prod_dt between '01-jan-24' and '01-dec-24'

and v.plant_no in ('PIPPT', 'SIMPT', 'WAPPT')

and v.comp_cd is null

and  p.ctr_party_ba_no is not null

and p.acct_mtr_type_cd = 'SL'

and NOT EXISTS (

   SELECT 1

   from qrmtips.qpost_alloc_vol v2

   join qrmtips.qpost_paystation p2 on p2.trnx_id = v2.trnx_id and p2.mtr_sfx = v2.mtr_sfx

   left join qrmtips.qctrl_ba_entity e2 on e2.ba_no = p2.ctr_party_ba_no

   where v2.prod_dt between '01-jan-24' and '01-dec-24'

   and v2.plant_no in ('PIPPT', 'SIMPT', 'WAPPT')

   and v2.comp_cd is null

   and  p2.ctr_party_ba_no is not null

   and p2.acct_mtr_type_cd = 'SL'

   and  v.plant_no = v2.plant_no

           and v.prod_dt = v2.prod_dt

           and v.unit_tm_cd = v2.unit_tm_cd

           and v.mtr_no = v2.mtr_no

           and p.mtr_nm = p2.mtr_nm

           and v.mtr_sfx = v2.mtr_sfx

           and p.ctr_no = p2.ctr_no

           and p.ctr_party_ba_no = p2.ctr_party_ba_no

           and e.ba_nm1 = e2.ba_nm1

           and p.acct_mtr_type_cd = p2.acct_mtr_type_cd

           and v.rec_status_cd = v2.rec_status_cd

           and v.prod_cd = v2.prod_cd

           and v.disp_cd = v2.disp_cd

           and nvl(v.comp_cd, 'x') = nvl(v2.comp_cd, 'x')

           and v.vol_type_cd = v2.vol_type_cd

           and v.gas_vol = v2.gas_vol

           and v.heat_value =  v2.heat_value

           and v.liq_vol = v2.liq_vol

           and v.theo_gas_vol = v2.theo_gas_vol

           and v.theo_heat_value = v2.theo_heat_value

           and v.theo_liq_vol = v2.theo_liq_vol

           and v.other_qty = v2.other_qty

           and v.pct_contr = v2.pct_contr

           and v.alloc_grp_no = v2.alloc_grp_no

           and v.alloc_seq = v2.alloc_seq

           --and v.run_id = v2.run_id

           and p.phys_ctr_cd = p2.phys_ctr_cd

item.title: [DF-280] Cleanup v2 tables in keyera_sustainability_* catalog
item.description:
The workflows have been using v2 and no workflows have used the original versions of the tables for a while. The v2 tables should be renamed to just the table name to avoid confusion (e.g. silver_air_emissions_v2 → silver_air_emissions).

Tasks:

  1. Rename v2 tables to just the table name, making sure data and permissions remain the same.
  2. Update downstream emissions workflows that rely on these tables so that they do not use the v2 tables.
  3. Update emissions dashboards so that they do not use v2 tables.
item.summary: Cleanup v2 tables in keyera_sustainability_* catalog

item.title: [DF-257] Add Environment Name to the Databricks Dashboards Name and remove _vXX.lvdash.json from dashboards/
item.description:
Since Databricks now supports Git version control for dashboards, the emissions_detailed_emissions_v1,v2…..lvdash.json dashboards are now recognized as Dashboards by Databricks instead of just json files.

This was causing conflict issues in the deployment pipeline (screenshot #1) as it couldn’t seem to write the old jsons into the keyera-databricks-emissions-dev/files/dashboards folder. After deleting the old dashboard jsons in dev and manually redeploying, it fixed the issue. After running the pipeline however it now imports all the old lvdash.json files as dashboards, clogging up the Dashboards screen (screenshot #2). To fix this, we’ve decided to delete the old _vx.lvdash.json from the source code and rely on Git to restore previous versions.

screenshot #1

screenshot #2
item.summary: Add Environment Name to the Databricks Dashboards Name and remove _vXX.lvdash.json from dashboards/

item.title: [DF-236] LI Contracts & Amendments Processing
item.description:
Why

We have large numbers of contracts and amendments that we need to understand and analyze in aggregate.

How

How do we propose solving this problem with data?

What

What are the specific deliverables?

Requirements

Use the questions below to guide business requirements. In combination with our Technical Standards, these form the functional and non-functional requirements.

  • Define
    • What data do we think we need to solve the business problem?
    • What other factors besides data might need to be addressed to solve the problem?
  • Ingest
    • What sources have the data that we think is needed?
    • What are the characteristics of the source data that we need to be aware of (e.g., refresh cadence, quality, granularity)?
    • Are the data sources relatively easy to access or do they require extra development to connect (e.g., is it an internal system with an accessible database, does it have an object model that makes it difficult to query, do we need to pull the data from an API and do we have access)?
  • Transform
    • What is the shape of the source data and what shape is needed in the final product?
    • How clean is the source data and does it conform to Keyera standards (e.g., quality, units of measure)?
    • Does the data need to be normalized or joined with other data sets to be useful?
  • Process
    • Is the source data already well understood, or does it require exploration and manipulation by a senior data analyst?
    • Is a single set of final “gold” tables sufficient, or is there value in providing access to some intermediate date sets?
    • How will the data be used (e.g., internal analysis, machine learning, presentation to end users)?
  • Consume
    • Who is the audience for the data?
    • Does the data include sensitive or confidential information?
    • How does the business intend to consume the data (e.g., Excel, Power BI, Databricks Dashboard, or will it feed into another system)?
item.environment:
The following information is necessary to complete setup of the business and data access packages:

  • What team owns the data?
  • What is the sensitivity classification of the data (Public, Internal, Confidential, Highly Confidential)?
  • Who is the business owner (1-2 specific individuals)?
  • Who is the business steward (1-2 specific individuals)?
  • Who are the business approvers (1-2 specific individuals)? Usually the same as business steward.
  • What Power BI workspace does this data need to be available in?
item.summary: LI Contracts & Amendments Processing

item.title: [DF-154] Gold 6: FCTT Offloads and Samples Dashboard
item.description:
Data source

Gold 1: FCTT Offloads and Samples table

Parameters

  • Product (default - C3, user-definable)
  • Offload date (default - current month, user-definable)
  • BOL range (optional, no default value)

Widgets

item.title: [DF-119] Ingest Sharepoint data as strings into bronze and move data enforcement to silver
item.description:
Why:

  1. We have a few columns that do not have the correct data type. See Wapiti Testing Log - Data Foundations - Confluence for data issues encountered so far. This story is aiming to address most if not all the issues encountered in the log so that these types of issues do not happen again.
  2. Currently when the script creates a new table in bronze, it assumes the data type of all the columns. If a column is blank at the time the table is created, the ingestion script may create the column as a numeric type even though it should be a string. This is now causing some issues with the new Wapiti data as columns that were previously blank now have strings in them. Ingestion then fails because the table is expecting an integer.

What:

  1. Pull all data into bronze as strings. Move data validation into silver instead.
    1. Bronze
      1. Pull all data as strings. Keep null values.
      2. Still clean column names. Current way works.
      3. Filter out records that have all nulls across all columns.
    2. Silver
      1. Enforce proper data types
      2. Enforce null checks. e.g. if there is a null value in gas composition, set it to 0
      3. Enforce composite keys (scd2)
  2. Recreate all the bronze and silver sharepoint tables.

Impact:

  1. We will have to delete and recreate bronze and silver sharepoint tables in each workspace on deployment.
  2. Historical audit data from before will be lost.
item.summary: Ingest Sharepoint data as strings into bronze and move data enforcement to silver

item.title: [DF-117] FCTT Month End Preparations
item.description:
What is the problem?

FCTT month end process is run manually through Excel. It starts with collecting data from Dearman, eOne and Comp Match, ensuring the sync of data across these three systems, running calculations and producing a set of customer-facing documents, and providing data on customer billing to eOne. These are manual step, time-consuming and error-prone, and includes a lot of communication and coordination of effort for Logistics, Plant Accounting and Measurements.

This data then become input into more calculations for FCTT balancing.

This process is expected to be entirely developed in EnergySys. While data EnergySys holds some of the data, it requires data intakes from Dearman, eOne and Comp Match. The processing of this data in EnergySys before it is ready for calculations is a significant effort.

How will we solve it?

Using Databricks as a shared visual space for Logistics, Plant Accounting and Measurements to see data discrepancies will be a huge step towards efficiency and accuracy of the FCTT month end process. We will need to compare Dearman, eOne and Comp Match data and identify discrepancies between any critical parameters, so that each business group can participate in the investigation. The resolution of discrepancies will be done in the source systems: Dearman, eOne and Comp Match.

Users will require an ability to re-load the data on demand (for example, after correcting data in the source system), as month-end processes are time-sensitive.

Once all discrepancies are resolved, users will be able to export several data sets to EnergySys. The additional benefit of this work will be preparing the data for EnergySys. This will significantly reduce the cost, effort and risk of EnergySys development for FCTT month end.

All data has been classified as “Internal” sensitivity.

Data stewards and access approvers have been identified as ? and ?.

item.title: [DF-112] Comp Match Data Access for Business
item.description:
Link to Details: Comp Match

What is the problem?

The business (Measurements) requires regular access (several times a day) to Comp Match data. Due to the residency of this data in the OT network, the access needs to be facilitated by IT. This state implies constant dependency of business users on IT resources, for whom this work is mostly a disruption. Additionally, passing the results to the business relies on multiple manual steps, such as running data queries, entering query parameters, copying and pasting data, which is error-prone. Any errors can have significant financial and reputational cost to Keyera.

What is the value of resolving this problem?

Providing business users with access to this data through Databricks can resolve the above issues of business dependency, IT work overload and the risks associated with human errors. In addition to the Measurements group, this information is required by Logistics and BD groups.

Why is/isn’t this work urgent?

Urgent for two reasons:

  • Long overdue promise to the business to provide them with independent data access
  • Freeing IT time, currently taken to facilitate data access for the business

How will we solve it?

Dashboards with graphics and lists will be created for each data set that is currently generated by IT for business users. Users will be provisioned with access to the dashboards, some with limited view-only access, others (early adopters) - with ability to create their own dashboards.

All data has been classified as “Internal” sensitivity. Data steward and access approver has been identified as Schemida Bourgeois.

item.title: [DF-95] Create Business User Access Package
item.description:
Tasks related to provisioning data analyst access to a given data product are grouped into a “Business User Access Package.” The intention is to ensure that the business is equipped to quickly and easily take advantage of every new data product delivered. See the project Technical Standards for more information.

  1. Create a single internal, developer APP AD group (e.g., SG_ALL_IT_DF_<business_team_abbrv>ALL_APPS_DEVELOPER<IN|CF>) to secure the PowerBI workspace, the compute clusters, and the writable unity catalog location.
    1. Note: This is required per team, not per data product.
  2. Create a PowerBI workspace for the business team to publish and share visualizations created in Power BI.
  3. Create a Unity Catalog location (e.g., keyera_sandbox_<business_team>) to allows the business team to save queries, notebooks, and tables within the Databricks (Lakehouse-Production) workspace.
  4. Create required compute clusters (SQL and General Compute) specific to the business team allowing read and write, attached to the appropriate workspace. Clusters must be tagged (at minimum) with "cost_centre" = "<business_team>". Cost policies must be applied to each cluster limiting usage to CAD $100 / day / cluster.
item.summary: Create Business User Access Package

item.description:
Link to Story Details:

2025may7 jy created/based from wolocationcost rpt

-- WAPITI INVENTORY ISSUE 

select 
	workorder.parent
	,workorder.wonum
	,workorder.siteid
	,workorder.description
	,workorder.istask
	,workorder.worktype
from workorder 
where wonum = '5322471'

select 
	workorder.parent
	,woancestor.wonum
	,woancestor.siteid
	,workorder.description
	,workorder.istask
	,workorder.worktype
from woancestor
left join workorder on woancestor.wonum = workorder.wonum and woancestor.siteid = workorder.siteid
where ancestor = '5322471'

select 
	wo.wogroup
	,wo.wonum
	,wo.istask
	,wo.status
	,wo.statusdate
	,wo.description
	,wo.location
	,wo.reportdate
----	,locations.key_hierarchypath
--	,wo.key_craft
--	,wo.worktype
--	,wo.actfinish 
--	,wocomp.wo_compdate 
--	,wo.wopriority 
	,wo.glaccount as wo_glaccount

	,woactuals.actualstype as actuals_type
--	,woactuals.refwo
--	,woactuals.siteid
	,woactuals.directissue actuals_directissue
	,woactuals.itemnum as actuals_itemnum
	,woactuals.itemdescription as actuals_description
	,woactuals.linetype as actuals_linetype
	,woactuals.quantity as actuals_quantity
	,woactuals.unitcost as actuals_unitcost
	,woactuals.linecost as actuals_linecost
	,woactuals.gldebitacct as actuals_gldebitacct
	,woactuals.transdate as actuals_date
	,woactuals.ponum as actuals_ponum
from 
workorder wo 
left join 
	locations on wo.location = locations.location and wo.siteid = locations.siteid 
left join 
( 
	select min(changedate) as wo_compdate, wostatus1.wonum, wostatus1.siteid
    from wostatus wostatus1 
    where status = 'COMP'
    group by wostatus1.wonum, wostatus1.siteid
) as wocomp on wocomp.wonum = wo.wonum and wocomp.siteid = wo.siteid 
left join 
( 
  select -- select top 100 * from matusetrans where issuetype = 'RETURN'
    'MATERIALS' as actualstype 
	,refwo
	,siteid
	--isnull(storeloc, 'No') as DirectIssue--
	,CASE when storeloc is not null then 'No' else 'Yes' END as 'directissue'
	,linetype
	,matusetrans.itemnum
	,item.description as itemdescription
	,issuetype
	,quantity
	,unitcost
	,linecost
	,gldebitacct
	,actualdate as transdate
	,ponum
  from matusetrans 
  left join item on item.itemnum = matusetrans.itemnum 
  where refwo is not null
UNION ALL  -- select top 100 * from servrectrans
  select 
    'SERVICES' as actualstype
	,refwo
	,siteid
	,'' as 'directissue'
	,linetype
	,servrectrans.itemnum
	,item.description as itemdescription
	,issuetype
	,quantity
	,unitcost
	,linecost as linecost
	,gldebitacct
--	,loadedcost as 'linecost'
	,transdate
	,ponum
  from servrectrans 
  left join item on item.itemnum = servrectrans.itemnum
  where refwo is not null
UNION ALL 
  select 
    'LABOR' as actualstype
	,refwo
	,siteid
	,'' as 'directissue'
	,transtype as 'linetype' -- select top 100 * from labtrans
	,labtrans.laborcode as itemnum
	,craft as description
	,'' as issuetyype
	,regularhrs 
	,payrate
	,linecost
	,gldebitacct
	,startdate as transdate 
	,ponum
  from labtrans 
  left join labor on labor.laborcode = labtrans.laborcode
  where refwo is not null
  
  ) woactuals 
		on woactuals.refwo = wo.wonum 
    	and woactuals.siteid = wo.siteid 
  where 
    1=1
	--and wo.status in ('COMP','CLOSE') 
	and exists (select 1 from woancestor where ancestor = '5322471' and woancestor.wonum = wo.wonum and woancestor.siteid = wo.siteid )
    --and wo.location in (select location from locancestor where ancestor = 'KETTM')
    --and wocomp.WOCOMPDATE between '2021-11-05' and '2022-11-05'

order by wo.wogroup, wo.wonum asc, woactuals.actualstype

item.title: [DF-89] Review performance results with DBA + DF Team
item.description:
i want to ensure we have a step in the "one page plan" to include "efficient stage/replicate" – at present i havent decided if databricks can do it efficiently. 

 

i found a sql performance analysis i did on maximo server before we implemented: SQL cluster with dedicated reporting node and seperate cached storedproc linked server to further offset load.  

  • i want to make sure the Ingestion/Extract process is efficient and/or we include staging or replicating the data because maintaining the integrity and performance of the production systems is important.  
  • in the top cpu graph for the APP server, you can see avg cpu usage around 9% (500 to 750 mhz).  
  • in the bottom cpu graph for SQL server, you can see constant cpu usage at 40% even on the weekends (jul31-aug3 where APP is at near zero) – contributing to climate change and poor application performance at the time.
    • changes have since been implemented to limit climate change and improve performance.  

doing full table loads and model rebuilds every 30minutes is not efficient.  you might also say 40% is "low" – this was at a time when we increased the cpu from 2vcpu to 4vcpu on a DEDICATED sql server.  when you review the realtime cpu logs by vcpu/thread, the reporting service accounts were consuming 100% of 1.5 vpus.  

 

 

here you can see what happens if a poor report/model (in this example via powerbi) runs for 4m51secs against our 4cpu sql server

vs maximo application opening a workorder in the UI

item.title: [DF-88] Maximo Work Order Cost Reporting Datasets
item.description:
REQUESTER: Tom Connell, Jay Retzlaff, Jennifer Tansem, Dave Gronendyk

REF INTAKE DATA REQUEST: via DataServices https://keyera.freshservice.com/helpdesk/tickets/296376

Sample dataset and KPIs: Report Request_Maximo_Data_Turnarounds.xlsx Report Request_Maximo_Data_Turnarounds.xlsx (OLD REV – see sharepoint link for updated)

Business Justification:

Thank you for taking the time to meet over the past weeks and walking through some of the intent and requirements for requesting this new report from Maximo. For next steps;

 

  1. I have a current request to be provided with a one-time data pull of the table/table fields easily accessible for the fields outlined in the report
    1. Specifics: filtered just to "Turnaround" Classification and the years Jan 01, 2023- Current. - This will allow us to mockup and create all the logic for the later data cube version. Establishing buy-in & Support. 
  2. Providing you with the screenshot (worksheet 1) in the attached request book, as well as some justification to further support this request. 

 

    Link:Report Request_Maximo_Data_Turnarounds.xlsx

mockup (from xls)

 

Justification:

The request is to access our Maximo work order reporting system so we can extract cost, schedule, and materials data for historical and current turnaround projects. I believe this integration will significantly enhance how we track and manage our projects moving forward.

 

Currently, we're spending considerable time manually collecting project data, which often means our stakeholders are looking at information that's already outdated by the time it reaches them. By connecting directly to Maximo, we can provide real-time visibility into job plan execution, schedule performance, and cost tracking. This means our team leaders and executives will finally have current information to make informed decisions rather than reacting to problems after they've already impacted our timelines and budgets.

 

What excites me most about this approach is its scalability potential. Once we establish this dashboard framework for our current projects, we can quickly roll it out to maintenance operations, capital projects, and even procurement activities. The beauty of using a standardized data structure is that we'll have consistent reporting across all departments, which will reduce training time and improve how our teams collaborate.

 

The strategic value here extends well beyond just better reporting. With real-time data flowing into our dashboards, we can shift from constantly putting out fires to preventing them. We'll be able to establish meaningful benchmarks at both equipment and unit levels, which will help us identify where we're performing well and where we have opportunities to improve. This kind of institutional knowledge will be invaluable for future project planning and resource allocation.

 

 

Thank you, and let me know if you have any questions!

 

 

TOM CONNELL

Turnaround Advisor, Project Assurance & Support

Technical

item.title: [DF-70] Create Business User Access Package
item.description:
Tasks related to provisioning data analyst access to a given data product are grouped into a “Business User Access Package.” The intention is to ensure that the business is equipped to quickly and easily take advantage of every new data product delivered. See the project Technical Standards for more information.

  1. Create a single internal, developer APP AD group (e.g., SG_ALL_IT_DF_<business_team_abbrv>ALL_APPS_DEVELOPER<IN|CF>) to secure the PowerBI workspace, the compute clusters, and the writable unity catalog location.
    1. Note: This is required per team, not per data product.
  2. Create a PowerBI workspace for the business team to publish and share visualizations created in Power BI.
  3. Create a Unity Catalog location (e.g., keyera_sandbox_<business_team>) to allows the business team to save queries, notebooks, and tables within the Databricks (Lakehouse-Production) workspace.
  4. Create required compute clusters (SQL and General Compute) specific to the business team allowing read and write, attached to the appropriate workspace. Clusters must be tagged (at minimum) with "cost_centre" = "<business_team>". Cost policies must be applied to each cluster limiting usage to CAD $100 / day / cluster.
item.summary: Create Business User Access Package

item.title: [DF-66] write query to generate metadata for base tables -> unity catalog++ metada gen?
item.description:
this is to provide each table with the “xls” unity catalog data.

using maxobjcfg and maxatribute to get the info. todo: populate each table with LongDescription to use to describe/update/unitycatalog each table.

TODO: wasnt able to generate the sql select in a single string so its a union for now

TODO: execute it for each table we are replaicating it for to populate the stuff we need to pop

/* 
PURPOSE: script generate, per table, metadata for maximo toable to load into databricks unity catalog
maxattribute is essentially the shcema for maximo db.  
it would be equiv or more than unity catalog in terms of metadata.  

-- create select statement from  attr table

NOTES:
- i havent seen what the unity catalog looks like and or how it is populated.  at present ppl pop via ui i think based on xls sheet or they create a script based on xls

revision
2025feb jy initial revision
2025june jy update for multi table and col specific to match the xls
2025jun20 jy added details from maxobject.  will get the headerdescription from long description. 
	TODO: populate the ld for tables we dont have defined. 
	note: im not typing it into xls just so we can type it into another xls to paste into another table in databricks/unitycatalog.  someone can copy paste this
TODO: to be fit for UNITY use
*/

declare @tbl nvarchar(100) ='TICKET';
declare @sqlquery as nvarchar(max);

-- get table info 
-- todo: populate the long description with bizness info as required
select 
	objectname objectname
	,description object_description
	,ld1.ldtext  object_description_ld
	,eauditenabled
	,classname
	,isview
	,persistent
	-- ,*
from MAXOBJECTCFG 
	left join longdescription ld1 on ld1.ldownertable = 'MAXOBJECTCFG' and ld1.ldownercol = 'DESCRIPTION' and ld1.ldkey = maxobjectid
where objectname = @tbl

select 
	--*,
	objectname
	,attributename
	,alias
	,title as ui_title
	,remarks as ui_f1description
	,attributeno
	,maxtype as data_type
	,length as data_length
	,required
	,persistent
	,primarykeycolseq
	,domainid
	,sameasobject
	,sameasattribute

from maxattribute 
where objectname = @tbl


-- generate pastable sql to 
select 'SELECT ' as SQLQUERY
UNION ALL 
(select 	
		--concat(',', attributename) as columnonly --, ' as ''', title,'''') 
		concat(',', attributename, ' as ''', objectname, '_', upper(replace(title,' ', '_')),'''') 
	from maxattribute
	where objectname = @tbl
	and persistent = 1
)
UNION ALL 
select concat('FROM ', @tbl)

-- generate executable string

select @sqlquery =
	'SELECT '
	+ concat(',', attributename, ' as ''', objectname, upper(replace(title,' ', '_')),'''\n') 
		from maxattribute
		where objectname = @tbl
		and persistent = 1


	
select @sqlquery
item.summary: write query to generate metadata for base tables -> unity catalog++ metada gen?

item.title: [DF-53] Enable force bundle deployment to environments
item.description:
Currently when deployed resources (dashboards, workflows, etc) are manually changed on the Dev/Test/Prod workspaces, the cicd pipeline fails due to conflicts in the bundle. As a result, a dev would have to do the deployment from their machine into the desired environment.

This issue has happened a few times with dashboards when a quick fix had to be manually done in production, or someone opens a deployed dashboard in Draft.

Proposed fix: Create three manually triggered, separate custom pipelines that would force deploy the bundle to Dev, Test, and Prod.

item.title: [DF-28] Create Venting Emissions workflow
item.description:
Why

Venting emissions comes from blanket gas, compressor seals, and analyzers.

  • Note#1: In the Equip to Analysis Lookup sheet, an allocated volume method column was added. Allocated volume method = 3, denotes the Rate method which involves calculating allocated volume = rate * equip hours. This calculation is already captured in the equip_alloc_volumes table.

What

Venting emission pre-requisites and requirements have been added in the attached excel file. Major steps include (steps defined in the excel):

Pre-requisites for Venting Emissions requirements:

  1. Add the Mol weight constants to the Gas Properties tab in Sustainability Dataset
  2. The venting analysis groups have been added the "meter to analysis group" tab in the sustainability Dataset
  3. The total volume for the analysis group has been calculate in <workflow name> with results placed in 'keyera_sustainability_dev.silver_air_emissions_v2.equip_allocated_volumes' table (see Note #1)
  4. Existing schema for keyera_sustainability_dev.silver_air_emissions_v2.emissions_compositional_grouping updated to include additional columns: mol_weight, mass_frac_co2, mass_frac_ch4
  5. Calculate the "Mol Weight" of each sample
  6. Calculate the "Mass Fraction of C02" for each sample
  7. Calculate the "Mass Fraction of CH4" for each sample

Venting Emissions Requirements:

  1. Create a new table: keyera_sustainability_<env>.gold_air_emissions_v2.venting_emissions_metrics.
  2. Calculate c02_emissions_t with the following calculation: Analysis group allocated volume * (Mol weight / Ideal Gas Constant) * C02 Mass Fraction
  3. Calculate ch4_emissions_t with the following calculation: Analysis group allocated volume * (Mol weight / Ideal Gas Constant) * CH4 Mass Fraction
  4. Calculate co2e_emissions_t with the following calculation: (c02_emissions_t *Global Warming Potential of C02 Constant)+ (ch4_emissions_t * Global Warming Potential of CH4 Constant)
item.summary: Create Venting Emissions workflow

Edit: I don’t think we’ll need prerequisite #2 (meter to analysis group mappings). From my understanding we don’t have metered volumes or engineering estimates as volume inputs for venting. The allocated volumes calculation only needs the equipment hours (sheet: equip hours and load) and rate (sheet: equip specifications).

item.title: [DF-19] Create ABGPI workflow
item.description:
Why

Wapiti reports on the Alberta Gas Processing Index (ABGPI) metric which uses weighted Petrinex and volumes.

Currently, sustainability uses the template below to calculate ABGPI. This metric is based on this template.

Quantity = volumes per month from Petrinex or q2 (metered)

  1. Petrinex volumes: manual_abgpi_configuration has the Activity and Product codes that make up each Module group. Each of the product volumes have to be multiplied by the Module Constituent Factor then summed up per Module group based on the Module Operator. Petrinex vols are in silver_petrinex.conventional_volumetric_data
  2. Q2 volumes: meter_to_analysis_lookup has the q2 meters that makeup each module (denoted by analysis group column). Volumes for each meter should be pulled from{{silver_air_emissions.volumetric_totals_by_emissions_meter_grouping}} and totaled per month. At the end there should be a volume per module (analysis group) per month. There is no need to multiply these vols by a module constituent factor.

Weighted quantity = quantity used for compliance cost calculations in Wapiti (replaces DISP m3OE)

What

  1. New table (gold_air_emissions_v2.abgpi_metrics) is created with ABGPI per month.
  2. A dashboard with Wapiti emissions using ABGPI instead of Petrinex towards compliance cost calculation. Keep Petrinex at Rimbey.
  3. Dashboard UI changes
    1. Rename “DISP (m3OE)” column in Compliance Summary to “Production Metric”. Add a tooltip that says “Rimbey (DISP m3OE), Wapiti (ABGPI tCO2e)”.
    2. Rename “Dispositions (m3OE, sum)” widget → “Production Metric”.

item.title: [DF-16] TIPS Volumetric Data by Customer
item.description:
• Business Owner: Nicole Symington
  • Business Lead: Melissa MacDonald

Melissa M updated this epic description on 2025-06-04. The older version of this epic has been moved to comments below.

Background/Overview

  • The G&P BD team needs access to the TIPS posted volumes data for the following reasons:
    • To see what our customers see. The QQ data provides information about what is being delivered to the plant, but the values are not allocated to customers and the NGL components are not broken out. Having this data will allows us to go into customer conversations with all the info they have and identify issues at the plant or with customer sooner.
    • Projection of TIPS data on to QQ volumes to estimate NGL components and customer volumes prior to the monthly TIPS data being posted. There is an approximately 6-week lag between the prior period data and current day. Tracking the customers volumes and NGL components are important for pipeline nominations and customer relations.
  • This is multi-step request that will need to be completed for Simonette and Wapiti before moving on the South G&P facilities.

Request

Workflow is outlined in the BD Customer Working Volume Projection excel file (Lee and Melissa built this workflow in excel to be a guide for the process to be built in Databricks). The steps are generally:

  1. Pull data from TIPS using the “Pull Allocated Volumes Posted 2” query (attached). This work is in progress (link to Jira)
  2. Recreate the table in the Customer WI for Posted Periods tab in the BD Customer Working Volume Projection excel file. Make this a gold table.
    • The purpose of this table is to sum the relevant components from the TIPS Posted Volumes table by customer and month. Additionally, NGL yields are calculated (volume of NGL/total inlet * 100%)
  3. Recreate the BD Customer Working Volume Proj tab in the BD Customer Working Volume Projection excel file.
    • The purpose of this table is to calculate the historical proportion of the customer's volume at the TIPS meter and the NGL yields. The historical proportions are averaged over a 1-, 3- and 6-month period so that analysis can be adjusted.
    • This table does not need to be published as a gold table, but will be used for subsequent steps of this analysis.
  4. Map/connect TIP meters to QQ meters. Example of this work was completed by Gladys/Melissa in the Meter Mapping tab.
    • The purpose of this table is to connect TIPS and QQ data.
  5. Recreate the Customer Work Vol. Projections tab.
    • The purpose of this data is to have an estimate of what the allocated customer inlet volume and NGL components will be based on the historical TIPS values. This will give us insight into facility operations and customer activity prior to receiving the Posted Volumes from TIPS (~6-week lag in data currently).

Desired Outcome:

  1. Gold table for Wapiti and Simonette (single table for both facilities) containing columns on the Customer WI for Posted Periods tab of the BD Customer Working Volume Projection excel file.
  2. Access to the data calculated in steps 4 and 5 above.

comments.comment: Melissa MacDonald Scott Drennan Melissa - I cleaned up the Epic description. Intent is to be clear on what we would deliver in this epic and what problem it helps to solve. Let me know any feedback.

Scott Drennan - for posted volumes, I have added the initial TIPS query, a converted Databricks query, and the results from both. TIPS results were provided by Annie as I don’t have production access to that source system.

Moving the older version of the epic into this comment:

What is the problem?

Today, data is processed and managed by different teams and varies from asset to asset with issues arising from the following problems:

  1. Limited access to customer volumes trends and insights found in the verified data from the TIPS Production Accounting tool.
  2. Real-time asset measurement and composition data is either underutilized or not readily accessible, hindering decision-making and customer engagement.
  3. Repetitive and manual processes taking time away from higher value tasks.
  4. Absence of a streamlined solution for visualizing historical customer toll data at G&P facilities.
  5. No efficient way to monitor customer activity in the market, leading to a lack of strategic visibility into the total value and growth potential each customer represents to Keyera_._

Why solve the problem?

  • Access to accurate and timely data will enhance the competitiveness of the G&P BD and Operations team by streamlining processes, saving time, and enabling data-driven decision-making.
  • Streamline G&P data management, starting with plant volumes, to enhance daily workflows and enable data-driven decision-making.
  • Visualization of trends to identify opportunities for business growth.
  • Provide access to data as soon as it is available
  • Create consistency across all North G&P assets.

Why is/isn’t this work urgent?

G&P BD lacks necessary insights during customer engagement; this work will assist in driving revenue and improving margins.

How will we solve it?

This epic focuses on improving access to historic monthly Customer Volumes data for G&P BD. To do so, the following will be done:

  • Posted Volume, deduction, and meter hierarchy data will be extracted out of TIPS and brought into Databricks
  • Table and column metadata will be defined and loaded
  • Governance data (data owner, data steward) will be decided upon and documented
  • Security will be setup for all data products
  • A business access package will be deployed for the G&P BD analyst team to give them the required toolset to interact with data in Databricks
  • A Freshservice provisioning workflow will be implemented to allow people to request, and data stewards to approve, access to the data products

ARCHIVE BELOW ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

WHY:

The current process for aggregating monthly plant volumes requires exporting multiple reports from the SAP accounting software. BD Representatives then transform this data to summarize the volumes of raw gas entering the plant, along with the processed volumes of sales gas, NGLs, water, and acid gas. Without TIPS data BD reps are do not have insight into the NGL volumes at the plant or how much each customer is bringing to the plant,

This initial work will be used as a foundation to estimate the customer’s proportion of inlet gas entering the plant daily when it is paired with QQ data (link to JIRA). This will allow for BD reps to estimate volumes using QQ data instead of having to wait 6 weeks for TIPS data.

WHAT/DELIVERABLE:

Gold table metadata definition: GP_Business_Development_Product_Metadata.xlsx

Gold table: @Melissa to link (done!)

REQUIREMENTS:

Refer to linked user stories under product definition.
