item.title: [DF-11] Dearman Logistics Data
item.description:
• Business Owner: Shivaughan Sky
  • Business Lead: Melody Ho

What is the problem?

The business requires visibility of truck terminal data stored in Dearman.

There are requirements that were communicated to Emmett and Annie. Melody indicated that the current Dearman data does not fulfill all of them.

Melanie Quon, Svetlana Garaev can you help me find these docs?

The existing Dearman report in Power BI is used by BD reps as part of their nominations process. It relies on eOne data that needs to be refreshed hourly. Dearman refresh currently runs nightly. I believe eOne is the same.

There may also need to be additional cleaning of the data to eliminate duplicate BOLs. Dearman has logic that combines or eliminates these duplicates. It sounds like the data we are currently pulling from Dearman has these duplicates, so we need to determine if and how we can pull the deduped data from Dearman itself.

The existing Power BI report also includes row-level security because it is published to external users from different clients (like EnergySys).

Melanie QuonI think I’ll need to book some architecture convos to determine whether Databricks is the right system to provide real-time, externally published reporting. Databricks is essentially used for analytics, and our security model for Databricks is based on using it for internal and confidential data only.

How will we solve it?

Each item in this section will generally become a user story.

  1. Publish the requested to keyera_enterprise_<env>.gold_dearman.
  2. Load meta data for all tables (Logistics_Product_Metadata.xlsx)
  3. Create a single internal, viewer, DATA AD (SG_ALL_IT_DF_LOG_ALL_DATA_VIEWER_IN) to secure keyera_enterprise_<env>.gold_dearman and keyera_enterprise_<env>.silver_dearman
  4. Create a FreshService catalog item (approver: TBD) for access requests
  5. Create a PowerBI workspace for the Logistics Analyst team to publish and share visualizations created in Power BI
  6. Create a Unity Catalog location (keyera_sandbox_logistics) to allows the PA analyst team to save queries, notebooks, and tables within Databricks (Lakehouse)
  7. Create a require compute clusters (SQL and General Compute) specific the Logistics Analyst team allowing read and write
  8. Create a single internal, developer APP AD group (SG_ALL_IT_DF_LOG_ALL_APPS_DEVELOPER_IN) to secure the PowerBI workspace, the compute clusters, and the writable unity catalog location.

item.title: [DF-1] Wapiti Emissions Workflows
item.description:
What is the problem?

The business wants to expand reporting on emissions by building on the work done for Rimbey and expanding it to Wapiti. An in-person session at Wapiti on May 28th provides an excellent opportunity to share data the project’s work on emissions data automation with the broader organization.

Our roll out of the Rimbey and Wapiti emissions data dashboard will follow a few months of successful quantification and replication of compliance calculations.

What is the value to the business if we solve this problem?

We will use the dashboards for accruals going forward, and give access to select operations personnel. Operations will be able to use near-real-time emissions metrics to run tests and pilots on efficiency and emissions reduction projects, and to make quick and informed data driven decisions. The dashboards provide more granularity for operations and supporting groups, which will continue supporting Rimbey, Wapiti, and other facilities in identifying new opportunities for more efficient operation.

This will also allow us to decommission our existing time consuming, Excel-based calculators; it will also allow us to cancel contracts with Envirosoft, as we will no longer need to replicate emissions estimates to prove their reliability for compliance.

Why is/isn’t this work urgent?

This work follows on from the Rimbey emissions pilot. It is necessary to get us closer to a clear and timely picture of our emissions and related costs.

How will we solve it?

Add Wapiti data into the current emissions dashboard for automation of emissions metrics with required workflows to be presented on May 28th at Wapiti site to Operations, Maintenance, BD and Ops T teams. Two new emissions calculation workflows are new to Wapiti and need to be developed into the existing pipeline:

  • ABGPI Workflow
  • Venting Workflow

Further, emissions calculations already previously developed for Rimbey will be reused for Wapiti. These include: 

  • Fuel Gas Combustion emissions
  • Electrical emissions
  • Fugitive emissions
  • Flaring emissions
  • Liquid Fuel emissions

This will require validating and adding business metadata into Unity Catalog.

For this data product, the following access will be provisioned:

  1. Business User Access Package (for the Sustainability Team)
  2. Data Product Access Package (to secure viewer access to all gold tables)

Tables should be created at keyera_sustainability_<env>. All data has been classified as “Internal” sensitivity. Data stewards and access approvers have been identified as Colton and Rekha.

Acceptance Criteria

  1. A Detailed Emissions dashboard for Wapiti emissions is created, showing key metrics (fuel gas combustion, electrical, fugitive, flaring, liquid fuel, ABGPI, venting) that roll up into the compliance summary.
    1. Supporting data (production inputs and emission details) used in calculations are included, referencing the existing dashboard format.
  2. A dashboard with an Operations team view for Rimbey is created, showing relevant emissions trends for operations.
  3. A dashboard with an Operations team view for Wapiti is created, showing relevant emissions trends for operations.
  4. Dashboard(s) access is secured via an AD group, and users can request access via FreshService.
  5. Rekha and Colton have access to the dashboard.

Definition of Done

  • All DoD Criteria for associated user stories and tasks have been completed and signed off.
  • Business UAT Completed
  • Business Sign-off received

item.title: [DF-52] Automate Export of Daily Raw Meter Volumes for KAPS
item.description:
Overview

Schedulers (Derek Kam) complete a daily upload of raw meter volumes into EnergySys to support daily scheduling and monthly actualization.

As-Is

Schedulers receive data by email from Field Measure Coordinators and enter the data into a spreadsheet. There are typically 19 records per day with fewer than 10 fields. The primary key for the data is a Meter ID field, with data following the pattern “FIT-#####”. Multiple days of records may be imported at one time. The scheduler uploads the data to EnergySys using the I 9999 workbook, and the data is populated into the Daily Raw Meter Volumes table.

An example of the existing data import worksheet has been attached to this story.

To-Be

Each day, data for the previous day will be extracted from the keyera_measurement_prod.gold_volumetrics.final_measurement_data table, cleaned and processed by a notebook, and saved to a .csv file in a SharePoint location. The EnergySys file connector will watch for the file and complete the import using the existing I 9999 process. Email notifications with attached .csv files will be sent to the schedulers at each step in the process as a manual check, but manual intervention will not be required to complete the process. Email notifications must be configurable so that they can be turned off or directed to different recipients.

A sample query structure (SQL) has been attached to this story.

Note: Further validation of both the query and its outputs should be completed before notebook development starts.

Other Considerations

This may be a good time to restructure the catalogs and schemas holding volumetric data from MMS. Check: Business Engagement - Metadata Output for developing insights on measurement data sets.
item.summary: Automate Export of Daily Raw Meter Volumes for KAPS
